My two main concerns are this: Is there jump scares, and a lot of them all things considered?
And: What type of cheating is there? Mc being cheated on and girl being hurt, mc being cheated on and the girl isn't hurt, or the mc is the one doing the cheating?
The only thing I don't do well with is lots of unpredictable jump scares and the girl being hurt in cheating scenarios. I've had a certain braveheart academy do that but it was obviously avoidable. I learned my lesson after that.

Okay so, I've watched people play DDLC before, that was obviously not what people expected. Any similarities there?
Then there is Scorn which is... very fucked up, but I barely reacted to anything I saw, like, at all. Iron stomach? Perhaps.
It's the jump scares that get me.
I've been around, seen things.

Honestly, I think if existential horror is more in the text format, I should be completely fine. The implication that this is a long game is great for me, but I question if it's worth it if my initial two questions don't yield favorable responses.

Oh shit, one more thing! Do beloved characters suddenly die unexpectedly???
Click to expand...
Now I'll actually be helpful instead of falling into my guilty pleasure of random obscure quotes.

1. There are no actual jumpscares (in the sense of something suddenly screaming at you and jumping at your face). There are some flashing images, but most of the time you have a warning for them, and since the focus of the game is its narrative in text form, you know it's coming 99% of the time.

2. There is cheating in many shape and forms, but none that hurt the mc. The mc enjoys the thought of girls he's seeing to be seeing other girls at the same time - not that it happens a lot mind you, but it does happen (sometimes in a forced way) - although all of them that get into a relationship with the mc have him as their number 1. There is no other man involved in cheating either, the only exception is within mc's past and during very psychodelic hallucinations, that might even be about the mc himself fucking the girls and he's just seeing himself as another person.

That being said, girls do get hurt in the course of the game. There are various degrees of sexual assault/blackmail/possession and so forth. Again, not by any dude, mostly because of supernatural events, and a few times due to other girls.

Finally, there is an ongoing theme of "maybe none of this is happening" from the start, that makes it difficult to ascertain to which degree someone can even get hurt, or how much of anything is real. So take that as you will. I'll say that at the very least none of these scenes have been there just for shock value nor a fetish. They all serve a logical purpose within their own arcs.

Edit: 3. Death is very debatable in this game for reasons that you'll naturally pick up during the story. You won't have to worry about anyone leaving you for good.

I'll address your questions and concerns, but in your own best interest (without trying to be too pushy) I would recommend to just go for it afterwards, the more detailed questions you will ask, the more will you rob yourself of the enjoyment of finding out the story by yourself.

Is there jump scares, and a lot of them all things considered?
Click to expand...
In my opinion that depends on what you consider jump scares. There are recurring audio cues, a static sound, that indicates that some fuckery is going on. There might be some flashy images suddenly popping up seemingly out of nowhere.
But I wouldn't say that the horror element in this game is focused on getting actively scared like in a standard horror slasher. It's mostly psychological and existential horror. With occasional gory scenes. Think of "trying to face your inner demons and feeling powerless to do anything against them as you slowly slip away".
The comparison with DDLC is fair. Think of it being similar to that game, but much further expanded plot wise and the horror aspect much more subtle and not as central to the identity of the game. Essentially this game is still a slice of life story, just with trauma and weird dreams, gods, etc. thrown in.

What type of cheating is there?
Click to expand...
The MC is not getting cheated on. Actually scratch that, there has been this weird discussion going on, mainly in the reviews for some reason, about NTR. I guess there might be one or at most two scenes that could be interpreted that way, but this is far from an NTR game, the MC is not in danger of being cheated on.
At one point in time you have the choice to initiate in a sexual relationship with a married person (whose partner is not shown in the game at any point so far) but this is avoidable. And the relationships you may choose to pursue with certain girls might appear exclusive to some of them. So some girls might get hurt to some extent. Honestly, I would be kinda surprised if that ended up to be the thing that bothered you the most about this game lol.
In general though, if NTR is one of your concerns, there are canonically (basically) no other male characters in the game - it is explained at the very beginning of the game why.

Do beloved characters suddenly die unexpectedly???
Click to expand...
There might be cock murder at some point in this game. That is all that I am willing to say.
But in all seriousness, the girls you see in the menu's character screen from the beginning of the game still exist and are all alive up to this date.

Subversion (one word) or the base verb (to subvert) means to take the conventions of a genre and go against them, twist them, or turn them on their side. This game is a subversion of the harem genre of eroge. Another possible word to describe it would be "deconstruction," though they're not the same thing, this game is a bit of both.

It takes a lot of the common and popular tropes of eroge -- harem, schoolgirls, an unrealistically large penis, etc -- and twists them. Sometimes it does this by removing the fantastical elements of the genre and injecting a dose of reality, sometimes it does it by making everything appear one way, only to pull the rug out from under you.

And to better explain what I mean by "game with porn, rather than a porn game," the sex scenes are a thing that happens, but they're not the purpose of the game. The game is a slow burn, and very story-heavy, and sex happens when it's appropriate, and there's quite a bit of it due to its length, but if you're looking for a quick fap this isn't the game. This is an attempt at eroge as art, rather than eroge as simple entertainment -- which yes, sounds pretentious, but here we are.

And if you're one to project yourself into the MC, this probably isn't the game for you. Or at the very least, do so at your own peril. The MC is a terrible person in just about every respect.

yes, it's from this event that we made the connection that Maya ran away from home after being molested by a family friend and was taken in by Akira. The bench/drink he offered her is likely where she takes him after their first box run, which she says that "it's the only place in town that has that particular drink". But, mostly, we think it's likely that their first meeting was there because it would make sense that she'd take him there to test his memories (as it would be one of the strongest places to take him).

The last part of that narration though was often taken to mean what would happen if Akira hadn't taken her home (to the tutoring place). Nice catch regardless. All of this might be a lie though, since we know that Maya shouldn't exist, and likely hadn't at first. So this could all be more a "Maya legend", that they believe happened, rather than something that actually did.

posts.content_html_raw:
I unfortunately read Subahibi in Japanese so I can't copy its phrasing mimetically like a pile of mysterious goo regurgitating something it ate years ago. But it went something like - keep running to the horizon! Because over those heights, out of sight, beyond the end that is the sky, lays the hill of sunflowers! And what is a sunflower but a parasite that follows the sun to grow and then remains frozen in place? It's important that the parasite stays in place once it's grown, facing where the sun was. And it's REALLY, REALLY important that the brain is wider than the sky. Because it's only through the cognition of an individual that limits form, or as some say, that gods form, or as some say, the sky becomes a wall rather than the infinite expanse of space. Our heads are as heavy as a god's. Himawari's name has all the significance in the world. The sunflowers watch as the moon shines upon our ascent up the hill towards happiness, sunawachi the Love-Filled Everyday. Ami's name feels more like a spiderweb to me, which kinds of catches on you and gets you sticky and stuck... but I would never be too hasty.

And it's also REALLY REALLY important that Lessons in Love is a critique of religion. Discourse regarding gods-this-and-gods-that should never forget the dripping mockery and scorn for all things religious within the game. Worshipping a god is a LIMITATION. Worshipping a god is a TRAP. It keeps you LOCKED in PLACE facing a certain direction. It keeps you STARING AT THE SUN until YOUR EYES BURN OUT and swirl infinitely in the misery of blindness. Not good! How will you climb the hill of sunflowers like that? How will you learn how to love??? Can you love a god? What happens if the god loves back? What happens if a god DEMANDS you live happily? Now that's a good question.

Anyway, in other words, the subjects above reminded me how much meaning can be derived by putting Subahibi and Lessons in Love up next to each other on diffchecker dot com. But I have to disguise it in ramblings to not just spoil Subahibi. If anyone hasn't read Subahibi despite the image of Subahibi on Sana's PC I will take this moment to recommend it. Not because I like it. I'm sorry, but I did not like it very much. If you guys think happy events are a drag, hooh boy, how about a game all about the doldrum boredom of eternal recurrence! But the symbolism makes it very meaningful in a Lessons in Love context. The only question for me is why he used Ayana as inspiration for Maya when Ayana was... oops! We can discuss that at a later time gentlemen.

Altho it looks like Subahibi was NOT a hit on F95... Very few posts. Maybe Scat-痔 (<---- this is FUCKING HILARIOUS for Japanese experts) should have released it in installments on patreon. But I see my good friend Skwada wrote a review for it. Good lad!

It's not explained in-game, as "red path" and "green path" are ways the fans have come up with to describe how the game tracks things.

If you go into the menu and look at the list of events, you'll see that the events you've completed will be highlighted in green.

If you miss the trigger for an event (for example, if you turn down one of the side characters sexual advances), the event will be marked out with a red line, and the name will also be red, indicating a missed event (the name also changes.

"Green Path" isimply means you're making choices that show every event in the game. "Red Path" means you're making some choices that blocked off events.

In the early game, the biggest way to wind up on the red path is to turn down Sara (Sana's mother) when she propositions you. This blocks off quite a few events for both Sara and Sana later in the game (they won't show as missed until you actually reach their point in the story, though). Turning down Ami is another major one. Generally speaking, saying no to sex will always result in missed events (obviously).

I mentioned in a previous post that doing a certain Chika event too soon will cause a lot of Rin's events to get missed. Later (in chapter 2) going on a trip with Chika before doing all the Yumi events from that update will cause a scene MUCH later in the game (chapter 3) to be missed. I'm sure there are others that I'm forgetting, but those are the big "how did I miss this" moments.

You can also miss events by not having enough Lust poitns with a girl. Not having enough Affection won't cause events to be missed (progress pauses until you have enough to trigger the event), but Lust determines whether sex scenes that trigger at very specific story moments happen or not. It's for this reason that most people here suggest using the Universal Ren'py Mod or a save file editor to alter values to a high number so you don't risk missing content.

DeanNoriko said:
Speaking of other threads, I noticed one thing that I found quite funny and interesting.
You guys know that we dunk on Selebus all the time, complaining that he is an arrogant dickhead and that he used to be a good boy who'd post in this thread before he became a pissy boy.
Looking at the Being a DIK thread, I found it very interesting, if not even surprising, that the general consensus was that Dr. Pink Cake (the dev of BaDIK) is a greedy asshole who used to be wholesome but turned on his F95 community and is now swinging the banhammer at people daring to say anything negative
Here is a quote from the user Better Cock Spock as an example (I really hope he does not mind me quoting him):

(There is a whole discussion about it going on in that thread if you want to check it out)

It's funny to me to see the parallels. We shit on Sel all the time, but I guess it might just be, to some extent, in the human nature to become an egocentric ass once the money starts flowing in big time. Sure, DPC is presumably making a lot more cash than Sel, but the change in demeanor still seems very synchronic.
It makes me almost forgive Sel a little bit, or at least understand him better, seeing that he is not an outlier apparently.
And you still gotta give him credit for being very reliable and punctual with his updates, he rarely misses content wise as well. Whereas someone like DPC is getting criticized for the longer and longer delays in updates (now over 12 months for the upcoming one, likely to go to about 14 or 15 months) and relatively subpar content as of late.
I'm curious to see what you guys think of this.
Click to expand...
I've actually seen another Dev with a similar story, the creator of Twisted World, a Trap, Futa, male/female role reverse game that was surprisingly really good and had really good models was up to update 0.73, game was going good, the story was entertaining and the MC was fun to play and read. Dev was getting pretty good money (No where near Sel but for where he lived he had said he was making more then his local doctors) his update were large and pretty consistent, longer updates taking a bit longer but well worth the wait. Admittedly though his last two updates were huge and had good scenes, the story had started to feel like it was losing quality and one big thing of the game was that every female was very top heavy, talking anime style bigger then heads and for the most problematic character bigger then her torso so he started having to deal with clipping issues (usually I would be turned off by comedic sized boobs but I enjoyed the game enough to look past it). At the time he was also very vocal about updates and issues which was good.

After 0.7 came out he had started to express being unsatisfied by how the game was going and I think by this time he had started to beef with the F95 thread for his game as after the whole Patreon purge started to be a thing he moved to Subscribstar and while usually people were good about it, the game had gotten leaked before it's public release (He would release it for higher tier subs first). At this point he announced that he would take a break and remake the game, take a year to do all the hard stuff (Make assets, the map, programing etc) so that when he's ready all he has to do is put it together and release the new stuff, meaning faster updates. At the time he was pretty trustworthy and usually kept to his word (Though I think the first sign of issues was he had a tier on his pateron/subscribstar for $100 which had it's own issues) which most of us were cool with, and on his discord he was pretty good at keeping people informed about what was going on.

I think this is when the problems really started to happen, he had taken that year but never paused or stopped the money coming in (Or got his supporters to just go for lower tiers as he worked on the new stuff) and since he was still getting paid while just working on stuff in the background I think that changed his mind set, he started being less informative about updates, said he had finished the hard stuff midway through the year and was working on tweaking and coding (Which he is terrible at and refuses to hire someone to help cause he claims he had a "bad experiece" with a coder before so only wants to do it himself) come Nov of 2023 where he had claimed he had most of the assets and "hard stuff" done in June/July he finally annouced the first update to the remake, to be released around Christmas time as a present for all, but the date came closer and no info, the date was a week away and he said he had to dely due to family coming over and so had to push the release in Januray, Understandable but then Jan came, no information, Feb came and he said he was having issues but would release the update soon, I think by the end or Feb or around March he finally released the first update, which only had half of what he said he would release and from the guy who usually puts out around 1-2 hours of content at his smallest updates, this one was 15-20 minutes if you read everything and did everything. He then promised to get the second half of the update as soon as he can, at this point he also started to send his loyal modders of his discord to attack people here who were saying negative stuff and banning anyone on said discord that said anything bad, even in a joking manner. He has finally released the second half of the update but its missing scenes and looking like he's now expanding it with "new" ideas.

He went from 2-6 months per update (6 months being hours of content and lots of proper animations) to now it being almost two years since the first game's last update, one year from the first promised remake update and he's only released I think 2/3 of it. Everyone is upset, bashing him too the stars calling him a milker and acting terribly, he attacks F95, the place that got his game on the map and has bragged (In now deleted posts) he's making tons of money, more then doctors in his country. He also spends a lot of time making Koikatsu cards for extra money (During the year he showed off over 100 characters he made that he said will be showing up in the game) But yeah, reading about Sel reminded me of him. Funnily enough he also uses a S name, Snatz.

DeSkel15 said:
I recommend checking out the Wiki:
https://lessonsinlove.wiki/index.php?title=Main_Page

And just playing the game while doing what you want to, the first playthrough.

This is not the kind of game where you'll understand everything the first time (or probably even the 10th), and there are different dialogue and reveals depending on your choices, lust points, affection points, and the timeline of when you do certain things.

Then there's how future info will alter your personal perception of past info and vice versa, making replays more or less necessary, and we aren't even halfway through the game yet.

The "Green Path" is what it is called by fans when you don't have any Events with a red line through them, and they are all green, however there are things you'll miss no matter what you choose on one playthrough.

The Events themselves have variations whether you miss them or not. URM can reveal the variations throughout the game if you let it notify you on the paths, though.

Overall: Just play and have fun. I personally don't use any guide as I prefer doing everything at least once. I prefer the big picture.

Once you get caught up, then you can find (work in progress) timelines and theories here, without worrying about spoilers.
Click to expand...
I believe VoidExile doesn't generally replay. Though I he (he?) may find this game more suited to multiple playthroughs.

But VoidExile, if you don't want to plan on replaying, may I make a couple of suggestions?

  1. Bookmark a hexadecimal-to-text translation tool (ideally one that has some other cryptographic help). There are whole swaths of information hidden behind not-very-secure-but-thouroughly-annoying "code." (The wiki has most of those chunks translated, but not all, and it's not always a) up to date or b) easy to navigate.)
  2. Have some way of searching through the actual programing code. The .rpy files in the game folder are basically just Python-flavored text files. Having a coding tool of some sort will allow you to search quickly for particular strings of text and, for example, copy and paste those big chunks o' alphanumerics into that translation tool I mentioned above. FWIW, I use Visual Studio, because I already had it on my computer; anything that can search through a whole directory would work, though. At this point, I play with VS open in the background for when I am trying to figure out what the heck I just saw. I can track down a particular image that flashes on the screen for the blink of an eye, find alternate text that plays out, for example, if you ask a particular girl to use a certain nickname for you. All sorts of things.
Others have already suggested URM--I find it invaluable for not getting lost, but it did take a while to get used to. It does spoil the immersion a bit, but also makes it clearer what choices Selebus made, which I find interesting. YMMV

Decided to go through with this anyway. For convenience sake, I will be doing daily reaction spoilers like this one. So for obvious reasons, make sure you are ahead in progress if you don't like spoilers (I switched to autovn mod recently). This marks Day 1 of playing the game, technically day 2 as I started the game late last day.
Ehh, fuck it. I will just write... something that comes to mind as it comes.

Umm, since I got through day 1 before I started writing again:
I sort of understand the static and noise now. It's unexpected with a disturbing undertone but it's manageable.
The plot with 99% of men fighting in space is certainly odd.
There's a lot of fourth wall breaking and dark humor + the story is written in a certain way.
The list of students appear to be a huge mess with most if not all of them having some kind of problem.
Rin is probably my favorite so far other than Ami due to her hair and I guess the preview images.
And unfortunately I did reach that morning part... umm, okay, yeah, wtf?

EXCUSE ME WHAT WAS THE OBJECTIVE?... is this what people meant by it actively punishes you for thinking it's a porn or is that done in another form? I mean, this is what happens when you dream I guess so... could be worse, right?

Okay dude, now where did the head go!?

This game is gonna be wild if all sex scenes are like this. Never found myself laughing nervously so much while covering half the screen as much as now.

Everythings totally normal here he says... He didn't have a dream... nope, nothing involving the most fucked up sex scene I've ever seen... okay maybe I have seen something more fucked up... or have I? It's hard to tell.

These characters are way too open...

The humor gets me good!

...why did he let her go?

I feel like he should have spent a few more hours going by Ami how he usually teaches class.

Did the dev see all the games about reincarnating into another body with amnesia and go: No, I refuse to let the mc slowly remember anything about his past like by himself.

Not being allowed to have part time jobs while studying... wtf kind of rule is that?

I thought that closing your eyes thing was going somewhere else when he said he was about to force something...

Well that was entertaining. A little massage never hurt anyone. (I've never actually had one so I don't know...?)

Ahh good, I almost thought it was sponsored...
Why would I want costumes for Ayane's dad...?

I expected the mc to be worse tbh. Maybe I haven't quite gotten there yet.

Jericho 941... oddly specific I can even read the model name of the gun.

Why would I want three bonus coffins for a dead woman...?

Oh, well would you look at that. The infamous(or famous?) bathroom walk-in scene.
Haha! The reactions are so very different from other games.

"Any amount of love at all would be more than what I currently have for this girl..." what does this even mean? I feel like it's miswritten, or I just can't grasp it's meaning. Is it meant to say he can't love her more than he already does? Dunno.

A shrine is the last place I expected to see Maya working...

The existentialness of this existential horror game is certainly making itself known through the very complex and philosophical dialogues of these... teenagers. What...

Oh... I had a feeling Makoto worked at some interesting store, but I guess I didn't expect that kind.

It seems so far, my opinion of this game is highly positive despite it's quirks... which might actually be a good thing too.

Whatever god made him choose THAT dvd did it with a purpose.
I honestly expected it to backfire if you chose the student/teacher but that was even more hilarious than the others.

Ahh yes, I sure do love a (copyrighted frozen beverage). You really can't go wrong with a (copyrighted frozen beverage).

Wonder why he didn't tell Yumi about the new class changes. I mean she wasn't even there when they were discussed. Unless her friend supposedly already told her which wouldn't explain why she never mentioned it.

Why is that? A professional work uniform on a cute girl being cuter and a cute outfit on a cute girl? Is it the fact the cute outfit is distracting and the professional outfit is not and the professional outfit in some way also strengthens the person behind it making cute even cuter? Or perhaps is a fetish thing, who knows.

I really don't see how his methods would make sense. If there is one thing the story does that make me question things, it's definitely this. How can you be a teacher without actually teaching things? He even said no to helping Futaba study. I guess he wouldn't do much better helping her.

Will it ever be explained why his eyes are like that...?

Haven't had the static happening for so long I was almost caught off guard. It's weird. Still trying to figure out the pattern to it.

Futaba is BBW? Isn't it BWW? Or, neither, I dunno.

I totally expected to meet Miku or something at the dojo, not Ayane of all people... especially after they just said someone was approaching at a rapid pace, which is something I imagine a very energetic girl doing, aka Miku.

Sodomize Maya? Wth? She has some lively imagination to go making that accusation.

Honestly, I see absolutely no way to converse with Maya, I think that just means the dev have made an 11/10 attempt at making this feel as real as possible. She just really does not want to talk to you and the things the mc says to convince her to be willing to do that don't work, things that I would try as well like pointing out the fact it's irrational for her to be so against talking... Aalthough there is that looming tsundere vibe going on and tsundere's are naturally difficult to talk to because in a way the things you say already have an affect just that they act like it don't, which I guess would explain why her affection keeps going up. Maybe... she's just the real life version of a tsundere? I've never actually known how those are but I imagine this is sort of it.

Hermit crab racing? It's... it's an actual things... huh.

I hope he gets around to confirm how old he actually is.

Okay so, interesting tidbit, most of us regulars remember the iconic "three girls in a line, one calm, one callous, one concerned"
Mind you, this is way before Wires is even introduced. The Nozomu genesis was introduced, as was HOPE, but that's it. And yet here are the three gods.

Well, what caught my eye actually comes from the next one:
Day literally turns to night. And it says that the three gods disappear. Well, what if they really were there before then, rather than just foreshadowing? In later updates we'll see Yasu turning night to day (although that could simply be Akira slipping himself rather than the world), and even later we see the three moons looking down on Sana/Akira.

Maybe this is the start of it all? Three gods watching, Three moons watching, the event is called the moon is beautiful. It's all during beach episodes.

Edit: Oh, forgot to add that the implications if this were true is that the three of them do not switch out necessarily, but that they all are awake at the same time, and can observe at the same time. This would counter, for instance, that HOPE goes to sleep in underheaven during winter. Or at least that Wires would be awake during summer (which it is at this time).

And this marks day 2 of speeding through this game. I feel like I haven't even scratched the surface. 6912 characters worth of reaction text this time around.
Okay so, memories and consciousness is stored in the brain. Some interpret it as consciousness being stored in the soul which can be carried over to other bodies. Some interpret it as if both memories and consciousness is stored in the soul. So you would either remember everything from your new body or your old body and in some cases like in Dogma, both. In this case however... neither.

Oof, Ayane and Sana up to something cringey...

Making some progress with Ayane with that kiss. Nothing even noteworthy to react to there

Seems the first girl to reach 5 affection in autovn is Futaba, oddly enough.

Does autovn like to skip over affection events you have somehow already seen? I'm confused. I've accidentally scrolled backwards wanting to reread something and end up missing that entire scene because it gets skipped over it. Not sure if I actually miss something tho, probably not... Still get a sort of panicky feeling tho.
Often the game goes from going to visit someone at night to going home instead. If I were to make a wild guess, I would assume it does this to save you skipping time. The autovn is most likely a way to replay the game by skipping to the important game changing decisions.

Bringing a chicken to school is certainly not the weirdest animal you can bring, but it's definitely up there.

Rin having an interesting reaction to Chika's touch.

I don't like the looks of this dark school hallway...

What an absolutely vile sentence... "A pile of used up teenagers" Just no.

Somehow that completely normal smilie scene was disturbing to me. It's easy to forget this game is not what it seems when 95% of the time it's just slightly edgy every day life stuff.

Dude, I went outside to buy some things and I return only to get the first happy event... WHAT.THE.FUCK?
The game really just made me click through all those triple dots?

Okay, I just went and translated the text and hex decimal text. "am i okay" and "goodbye". I haven't done this previously with other text but I doubt it was important...

I wonder if that first nightmare we have could technically be considered a free happy event.

Oh, lovely. Arachnophobia. These aren't exactly the welcoming kinds either... I don't have arachnophobia but I still have a fear of spiders and these aren't exactly pleasant to look at.

No no, keep the happy song on (no, not THAT kind of happy, I mean the real kind). It's very soothing in this mildly distressing situation.

Oh, lovely. You know this game is so fucked up, I doubt I would actually care if one of the character died for real. Kinda difficult to form an emotional connection with a bunch of fucked up girls when all this is going on.

(insert multiple repetitions of the daisy daisy song here)

Maybe this is the time for me to start questioning if this game will really change me or if I will come out fine, like it was all an illusion.

This is gonna be real fucking interesting when I go to look in the image folder at some point.

The most distressing thing would be if this game decides to somehow "leak out". Becomes real...

Welp, I understand the popularity of the game now.

These happy events are... exhausting.

It just ended, just like that. As if he never even knocked on the door but thought he did and triggered this whole thing.

And that's either a real spider or a cgi spider... How lovely.

Well. Kaori seems interesting enough. Given what I've seen so far, I can't help but be concerned if this spider theme will evolve or not.

The only thing that sets this scene apart from other scenes is the fact Ayane just pulled out a gun in the middle of this roleplay dojo session. That's just the kind of ridiculous thing I would expect.

The room looks normal this time around. Good... very good...

You know, I wonder how normal this game would be if you removed everything that isn't actually real in the game such as the nightmares and happy events for example. What if someone made a mod that just entirely removes all that? That would be interesting. I'm sure if you can reorganize how the events trigger with autovn you should be able to just straight up skip some events entirely even if in a normal playthrough that is impossible. Perhaps that's a way to push out the game to more sensitive audiences. Of course it does remove the gameplay experience but that doesn't have to be a topic of discussion for another 6 or so years assuming this 33-40% took 4 years to make.

Wonder if we will figure out what's in the "don't open" boxes. It's either toys or something really disturbing, nothing in between. Alternatively they are just convenient decorations that will never be used.

Why are all these options bad? Looks is the generic option that people actively say is bad. Innocence is kinda creepy. Sex is also creepy. The game really setting you up for failure with this one.

posts.content_html_raw:
Upon this early morning dreary, feeling weak and weary, I found myself once again listening to a track of Good Kid on Youtube - most precisely, the video "Good kid - Bubbly [1 hour]" (4.4k views) uploaded by Horror 163 (544 subscribers). This is a particularly enchanting track for me due to the contrast between the upbeat rhythm and the rather grim lyrics. To quote: I never sleep, I never eat, I never leave my house alone. This particular chorus resounds in my head like shouts echoing within a cavern void of all but darkness. I find myself murmuring it to myself at idle moments. I never sleep, I say as I get in bed, I never eat, I say as I slouch in my chair, and I most certainly never leave my house, much less alone. But in these moments I am far from despondent myself: if Good Kid man never sleeps and never eats, why should I feel bad about it myself? It makes me feel enthused to continue existing, and I give my usual silent prayer of gratitude to Lessons in Love for introducing me to a life-defining band.

But invariably there will come a momentum of contemplation which interrupts the stillness, and in this case it's the community's overall poor reception to the Good Kid tracks. I have nothing bad to say about this in itself - I know one individual who loathes all music with comprehensible lyrics simply because he prefers the more primal enchantment of raw beats to thinking about any such poetry, and I can imagine that the erudite readers of Lessons in Love would have respectably eclectic tastes of their own. However I must say that the sheer vitriol directed at the update and music continue to perplex me to a degree, for while I played the tracks felt completely natural to me, and I found the music fairly good as well. If I had a complaint it was mainly that I felt, in retrospect, it was deceptive for Him to comment on this update having "the most new music on any update since such-and-such" which swelled anticipation for something much more original or unique than a series of Good Kid tracks.

Nonetheless, when reality does not meet your expectation that means one must "update their priors" as we Bayesians say, and I have done so, though my intention here is not to get into that too much. The unique playstyles individuals have go far beyond what can be covered in a brief F95 post - the psychology to vetting all music in a game's updates and deleting tracks which does not suit one's taste, for example, is worthy of a dedicated post. Instead, I thought - as good kid man sings into my ears 'I get the feeling I will someday die, and I'm not going to care' - that it might be fun to record some meditations on the inclusion of Good Kid in Lessons in Love.

The first observation I wish to note is the intriguing fact that Good Kid has official chiptune renditions of their tracks, which were later used in SENSEI QUEST (TM) as we all know. This is intriguing because with a flash of intuition it struck me that Good Kid's tracks in the previous Dorm Wars may have been chosen purely due to the existence of these chiptune tracks. We can imagine that the broad strokes of Sensei Quest being painted years ahead of time (perhaps as early as Dear You was written, though I would have wagered it gestating in His mind since a viewing of Oretachi ni Tsubasa wa Nai, had He seen it), and the moment the good kid chiptune tracks were released the idea snapping into place (them being released, to my knowledge, months after the launch of my game; We have noticed a tendency for Him to track all new releases of relevant artists, so perhaps He saw them as soon as they were uploaded, or perhaps He saw them only later). In any case, speculation of this nature is wholly meaningless as creative inspiration is like - as my Dear Beloved David Lynch would say - like catching a fish from the dark shadows of the mind. It can happen at any time, it is out of one's control, and all one can do is quickly write down the intuitions. Remember to write down your intuitions! The dark energies of the brain are beyond our control, and as the electricity surges all can be gained or lost.

The second observation is of more concrete meaning. Good Kid's lyrics are shockingly well-suited for Lessons in Love's themes. Now, this is something tricky, because I have over time found LiL's themes to be so fundamentally and universally relevant that they can be seen everywhere. For example, I recently watched Arawakawa Under the Bridge to see if perhaps the Arakawa family name was inspired by it, and while at first I was stricken by how perhaps such-and-such denpa was inspired by such-and-such idea, it later became extremely apparent to me that Arakawa is chiefly from Arakawa Naoshi, and BOY, if you want to see the inspiration for ideas, do I recommend watching Your Lie In April! HA HA HA!

That's a tangent though - the reality is that such primal themes such as mental illness, the seasons, etc, are universal to the primal human zeitgeist, and so phantoms of their presence can be seen anywhere. One must be wary of drawing lines between dots which ultimately form a grotesque creature rather than a divine symmetrical shape. However, in LiL's case, it's a fact Good Kid tracks were put into the game, and thus are worthy of special attention. To that end I have selected three tracks for our lyrical analysis: Summer, Second Rate Town, and Pox. I have implied analysis of Bubbly above - I trust the reader to determine the significance of staying inside all the time and having a lack of care for death.

Firstly, "Summer" should draw attention for its name alone, for of all the seasons we can say that Summer has presently been "The most important" in Lessons in Love in certain senses. Let us look at some choice lyrics:

I thought the world ended in March
Until I heard the doorbell ring
Can’t keep from falling apart
But I’ll glue back everything again

This can’t be the end
This can’t be the end
This can’t be the end
This can’t be the end
Of all that summer had to say
What little time has gone away

Much like killing frogs and jokes by dissecting them, I am wary about placing definitive interpretations for lyrics. Even if the lyricist were to have a specific idea in mind, it's important that art takes a life on its own and new meaning can be derived through different ways of looking at it. Thus what I offer here is only one interpretation which ideally would be used for fuel as future thought.

As made more clear in a post by the band, this is a song about picking up the pieces of yourself after you've fallen apart and accepting your flaws - including the parts of yourself you don't love. If one did not immediately recoil in realization as they draw a parallel from that to SeleGHAghaCOUGH COUGH from that to Sensei then I am uncertain what to say. The cycle of being unable to believe something is over (in this case: summer, perhaps his Hot Boy Summer, his time of turning around and having the happiest times with his students), to being determined to "piece yourself back together" to try again, etc, are all potently relevant to Lessons in Love. The song even references the wings of a sparrow - what this means honestly I don't know but it's a bird so you know has to be pretty potent. I could go on but we have two more tracks to glance at. (I recommend watching the music video for Summer; it honestly helps a lot with interpreting the lyrics).

The second track is 'Second Rate Town.' Now this one is a jam. Let's get right to the lyrics.


This is a first rate town
But all you ever notice are the ways it’s stretched too far
And it has been knocked down
Well some of us are still left here between the scars
When you look around all you ever notice is you cannot see the stars
This is a first rate town a first rate town you know
You just can’t see very far


Well it will fade as all things must
I loved you but you didn’t love me enough
Winter comes, the car will rust
I’ll start it up then always run a little rough

Obviously, my mind here is drawn to Kumonoami. One could certainly say that the town is stretched way too thin, and that Sensei is noticing it, though perhaps the more interesting aspect is the way in which the singer seems to be pleading with an individual to like a place more than they do - this song actually has two different titles, First-Rate Town and Second-Rate Town. Well, which is it? It's ambiguous, just like how Kumonoami is ambiguously a based town or not. You have certain individuals pleading with Sensei to love it there, while he may at times hate it there. Of particular interest is the background line "You can never leave," implying being trapped. Then there is "it will fade as all things must, I loved you but you didn't love me enough," which makes me think of either Sensei's trauma for Maya's suicide fading, OR Maya identifying that Sensei (as revealed by him choosing to abandon her when she got pregnant) didn't love her as much as she loved him. These are just tenuous connections, though, and not the purpose of the song. Nevertheless it's enjoyable to imagine this as a Kumonoami theme song of sorts. Of the songs played in LiL this one stuck out to me the most in the moment due to this.

The third track is 'Pox.' I chose this one purely because someone I know disliked all the Good Kid tracks, but said 'Pox' was the exception and the only one they liked. This may as well be random selection and will help prevent cherry picking in this analysis. I will now take a look to see what meaning I may derive.


My ancestral passage here
Was written down each year by year
But the map is too old, see they’ve forgotten the roads
And so we're living by the creases.

A pox, a pox, upon this town
I'd give it up just to burn it down
And if they die here you can blame it on me
I've been setting up gravestones in my hometown


Thoughts of particularly old repetition leading to a map aging to the point one lives by the creases rather than actively following any roads is intriguing - at this point in the game it is very distinct that the characters have rotten selective memories and kind of just ghost the lifestyle patterns they used to have, sometimes intentionally. Then we have more talk of 'towns,' the singer wishing a pox upon it, wanting to burn it down, and alluding to mass death (perhaps like the death of Sensei's class, though the details to this (barring a bus plummeting off a cliff) escape me; a favorite idea of mine is that after Sensei commits suicide, each of his class follows in turn because they can't live without his dick, though sadly it is also apparent that his over-sexualized body comes from his self-perception as a sex object rather than being an actual aspect of his true self).

Anyway, although it took longer than I intended, in the above paragraphs I gave examples of lyrics to demonstrate the clear thematic parallels of Good Kid's lyrics to Lessons in Love. It is a rather fitting band for the game, though I will again warn that many of these ideas are 'generic' (though I prefer the terminology 'aesthetically primal.') We could select a totally random band like Valleyheart, comb through lyrics, and point to lines like 'There's a knock on the door of my wavering troubled consciousness / and it's hard to ignore as the weather gets better outside / sure the blooming spring brings a brand new sense of accomplishment / what's the good if it doesn't feel right" or Take my worn out sense, make it new again / I think I've lost myself, can you heal my head?" However, in the broad scheme, I feel comfortable imagining the resonance He may have felt listening to good kid and the ideas He may have had when putting in the game, so claims that the songs are totally out of place seem disagreeable to me. Even were I not to like the songs, they give much food for contemplation and - to me - tie certain thematic knots in certain points of the long, long string that is The Game.

But is it not by lyrics that songs are most often judged; there is a strong tendency to simply absorb the sounds and then either smile or frown, with the former being a stamp of approval and the latter being a judgement of failure. This is another topic worthy of its own discussion: there is a STRONG tendency in critics to brutally tear apart a piece of media's story, visuals, etc, but completely throw their hands up at the music and say 'eh well I don't know about music so I can't say much but I like it / dislike it?'. This has perturbed me for a long time since it is so ubiquitous. I think there is a sort of mysticism to our resonance with air vibrations that compel even the most rational of analysis to mentally capitulate to magic and admit defeat. And arguably, this is wise of them, for rational critiques of music as produced by trained musicians are often bemusing - a friend of mine, for example, identifies the IV V iii vi chord progression with razor focus and cries on demand upon hearing it. That is a true story. However, it is hard to say a general audience will nod along and say 'Ah yes, this track was superb due to it's execution of the IV V iii vi chord progression.' In some saddening ways music is a firm bastion that continues to slay the ascent of Objective Critique.

I am no exception here. Not only am I not a musician, but I actively strive to avoid music theory in order to prevent myself from thinking in these concrete terms upon hearing music. Ignorance in this case may be bliss and if I open this Pandora's box it will be when I have exhausted more interesting topics. Nonetheless, I can say that Good Kid's tracks are pleasing to the ear and I found them enjoyable to listen to throughout the course of the Lessons in Love update. (I ESPECIALLY liked the chiptune versions present in Sensei Quest and left the game open for days at a time to listen to them before I realized that He had not arranged them himself and in fact I could just find them on youtube.) The problem is that this is lacking in substance to note; I may as well describe the strength of orgasmic bliss that rushed through my head as I ejaculated to a specific H-scene (answer: none. I have not whacked the mole to Lessons in Love a single time (nor did I discover it through h-scene tags) which makes me immune to approximately two/thirds of the fourth wall breaks.)

So instead I will try to scrape up a modicum of meaningful analysis. After hours of contemplation (again, listening to Bubbly - Good Kid) I have forged the shaky but perhaps meaningful idea that the Good Kid tracks provide valuable contrast. Ah, contrast, what a word beloved by critics and analysts alike! Let us ignore the desiccated skin of an overused term to instead identify what this means. After hundreds of hours of primarily ambient background tracks dotted by more contemplative, emotional tracks and distorted mockeries of them we are blasted with full-on upbeat indie rock so popular by the Youth that it is well-known for being officially included in the literal game Fortnite (to say nothing of the name of the band being literally Good Kid).

One does not be an analyst to notice this huge tonal whiplash. Indeed, it is this whiplash which has earned much ire! I saw one comment from someone aghast that after LiL consistently picked so many fitting, emotional tracks, the Good Kid update suddenly blew that all up will ill-fitting western music. But dare I say... that was the point? Okay, that is venturing too close to Happy Event apologism, so let me explain a bit. It's not like "being bad was the point." It's more like: what's going on at this moment? The class are performing a dorm war without Sensei. For a period they detach themselves from drama and are away from their depressive teacher. In the prime of their seething youth they engage in jubilant festivities and truly throw themselves at simply Having Fun, not to get in their teacher's pants, but to Have Fun - (indeed, those after the dildo take their leave). I would say this moment is so unique in LiL's history such a paradigm shift in music is more than fitting. It arouses excitement and energy in the class as much as us (keep in mind the music is wholly diegetic).

Consider an alternate reality where the dormitory war had a good - let's say great, even - ambient upbeat track to it. Some kind of vocal-free track not unlike ULTRA MEGA BATTLE THEME. This would have a pretty transformative effect; it's unlikely that the moment would have felt different or special, and it would run the risk of feeling more of the same, which would have likely been worse or less meaningful. Of course, we can only theorize at what other tracks may have been used, and I don't mean to say Good Kid was objectively the best choice. However, what I want to highlight is Lessons in Love is a game that is evolving and changing before our eyes, each new chapter a step into a new world. A bucket of cold water like Good Kid being splashed in our faces is precisely the kind of wake up call that a new paradigm calls for. Even those displeased by the reverberations are liable to remember it for months or years to come - and that, I find, is quite an artistic accomplishment.

Anyway, I think that's about all I have to say on this subject for now. The reaction to the Good Kid tracks continues to be as fascinating to me as the tracks themselves. Much like a mine rich in valuable ore, the more I contemplate it the more insight I seem to derive. I think those displeased by the Good Kid tracks may stand to benefit from spending 15 to 20 hours playing Good Kid's EP on loop while paying close attention to the lyrics and attempting to reach their inner child on Field Day. For now, I must give Good Kid EP 3 another listen since I've been biasing 1 and 4 lately. Its track Madeleine is rather interesting itself...

posts.content_text_full:
Upon this early morning dreary, feeling weak and weary, I found myself once again listening to a track of Good Kid on Youtube - most precisely, the video "Good kid - Bubbly [1 hour]" (4.4k views) uploaded by Horror 163 (544 subscribers). This is a particularly enchanting track for me due to the contrast between the upbeat rhythm and the rather grim lyrics. To quote: I never sleep, I never eat, I never leave my house alone. This particular chorus resounds in my head like shouts echoing within a cavern void of all but darkness. I find myself murmuring it to myself at idle moments. I never sleep, I say as I get in bed, I never eat, I say as I slouch in my chair, and I most certainly never leave my house, much less alone. But in these moments I am far from despondent myself: if Good Kid man never sleeps and never eats, why should I feel bad about it myself? It makes me feel enthused to continue existing, and I give my usual silent prayer of gratitude to Lessons in Love for introducing me to a life-defining band.
But invariably there will come a momentum of contemplation which interrupts the stillness, and in this case it's the community's overall poor reception to the Good Kid tracks. I have nothing bad to say about this in itself - I know one individual who loathes all music with comprehensible lyrics simply because he prefers the more primal enchantment of raw beats to thinking about any such poetry, and I can imagine that the erudite readers of Lessons in Love would have respectably eclectic tastes of their own. However I must say that the sheer vitriol directed at the update and music continue to perplex me to a degree, for while I played the tracks felt completely natural to me, and I found the music fairly good as well. If I had a complaint it was mainly that I felt, in retrospect, it was deceptive for Him to comment on this update having "the most new music on any update since such-and-such" which swelled anticipation for something much more original or unique than a series of Good Kid tracks.
Nonetheless, when reality does not meet your expectation that means one must "update their priors" as we Bayesians say, and I have done so, though my intention here is not to get into that too much. The unique playstyles individuals have go far beyond what can be covered in a brief F95 post - the psychology to vetting all music in a game's updates and deleting tracks which does not suit one's taste, for example, is worthy of a dedicated post. Instead, I thought - as good kid man sings into my ears 'I get the feeling I will someday die, and I'm not going to care' - that it might be fun to record some meditations on the inclusion of Good Kid in Lessons in Love.
The first observation
I wish to note is the intriguing fact that Good Kid has official chiptune renditions of their tracks, which were later used in SENSEI QUEST (TM) as we all know.
This is intriguing because with a flash of intuition it struck me that Good Kid's tracks in the previous Dorm Wars may have been chosen purely due to the existence of these chiptune tracks. We can imagine that the broad strokes of Sensei Quest being painted years ahead of time (perhaps as early as Dear You was written, though I would have wagered it gestating in His mind since a viewing of Oretachi ni Tsubasa wa Nai, had He seen it), and the moment the good kid chiptune tracks were released the idea snapping into place (them being released, to my knowledge, months after the launch of my game; We have noticed a tendency for Him to track all new releases of relevant artists, so perhaps He saw them as soon as they were uploaded, or perhaps He saw them only later). In any case, speculation of this nature is wholly meaningless as creative inspiration is like - as my Dear Beloved David Lynch would say - like catching a fish from the dark shadows of the mind. It can happen at any time, it is out of one's control, and all one can do is quickly write down the intuitions. Remember to write down your intuitions! The dark energies of the brain are beyond our control, and as the electricity surges all can be gained or lost.
The second observation is of more concrete meaning. Good Kid's lyrics are shockingly well-suited for Lessons in Love's themes. Now, this is something tricky, because I have over time found LiL's themes to be so fundamentally and universally relevant that they can be seen everywhere. For example, I recently watched Arawakawa Under the Bridge to see if perhaps the Arakawa family name was inspired by it, and while at first I was stricken by how perhaps such-and-such denpa was inspired by such-and-such idea, it later became extremely apparent to me that Arakawa is chiefly from Arakawa Naoshi, and BOY, if you want to see the inspiration for ideas, do I recommend watching Your Lie In April! HA HA HA!
That's a tangent though - the reality is that such primal themes such as mental illness, the seasons, etc, are universal to the primal human zeitgeist, and so phantoms of their presence can be seen anywhere. One must be wary of drawing lines between dots which ultimately form a grotesque creature rather than a divine symmetrical shape. However, in LiL's case, it's a fact Good Kid tracks were put into the game, and thus are worthy of special attention. To that end I have selected three tracks for our lyrical analysis: Summer, Second Rate Town, and Pox. I have implied analysis of Bubbly above - I trust the reader to determine the significance of staying inside all the time and having a lack of care for death.
Firstly, "Summer" should draw attention for its name alone, for of all the seasons we can say that Summer has presently been "The most important" in Lessons in Love in certain senses. Let us look at some choice lyrics:
Spoiler:
GK
I thought the world ended in March
Until I heard the doorbell ring
Can’t keep from falling apart
But I’ll glue back everything again
This can’t be the end
This can’t be the end
This can’t be the end
This can’t be the end
Of all that summer had to say
What little time has gone away
Much like killing frogs and jokes by dissecting them, I am wary about placing definitive interpretations for lyrics. Even if the lyricist were to have a specific idea in mind, it's important that art takes a life on its own and new meaning can be derived through different ways of looking at it. Thus what I offer here is only one interpretation which ideally would be used for fuel as future thought.
As made more clear in a post by the band, this is a song about picking up the pieces of yourself after you've fallen apart and accepting your flaws - including the parts of yourself you don't love. If one did not immediately recoil in realization as they draw a parallel from that to SeleGHAghaCOUGH COUGH from that to Sensei then I am uncertain what to say. The cycle of being unable to believe something is over (in this case: summer, perhaps his Hot Boy Summer, his time of turning around and having the happiest times with his students), to being determined to "piece yourself back together" to try again, etc, are all potently relevant to Lessons in Love. The song even references the wings of a sparrow - what this means honestly I don't know but it's a bird so you know has to be pretty potent. I could go on but we have two more tracks to glance at. (I recommend watching the music video for Summer; it honestly helps a lot with interpreting the lyrics).
The second track is 'Second Rate Town.' Now this one is a jam. Let's get right to the lyrics.
Spoiler:
GK
This is a first rate town
But all you ever notice are the ways it’s stretched too far
And it has been knocked down
Well some of us are still left here between the scars
When you look around all you ever notice is you cannot see the stars
This is a first rate town a first rate town you know
You just can’t see very far
Well it will fade as all things must
I loved you but you didn’t love me enough
Winter comes, the car will rust
I’ll start it up then always run a little rough
Obviously, my mind here is drawn to Kumonoami. One could certainly say that the town is stretched way too thin, and that Sensei is noticing it, though perhaps the more interesting aspect is the way in which the singer seems to be pleading with an individual to like a place more than they do - this song actually has two different titles, First-Rate Town and Second-Rate Town. Well, which is it? It's ambiguous, just like how Kumonoami is ambiguously a based town or not. You have certain individuals pleading with Sensei to love it there, while he may at times hate it there. Of particular interest is the background line "You can never leave," implying being trapped. Then there is "it will fade as all things must, I loved you but you didn't love me enough," which makes me think of either Sensei's trauma for Maya's suicide fading, OR Maya identifying that Sensei (as revealed by him choosing to abandon her when she got pregnant) didn't love her as much as she loved him. These are just tenuous connections, though, and not the purpose of the song. Nevertheless it's enjoyable to imagine this as a Kumonoami theme song of sorts. Of the songs played in LiL this one stuck out to me the most in the moment due to this.
The third track is 'Pox.' I chose this one purely because someone I know disliked all the Good Kid tracks, but said 'Pox' was the exception and the only one they liked. This may as well be random selection and will help prevent cherry picking in this analysis. I will now take a look to see what meaning I may derive.
Spoiler:
GK
My ancestral passage here
Was written down each year by year
But the map is too old, see they’ve forgotten the roads
And so we're living by the creases.
A pox, a pox, upon this town
I'd give it up just to burn it down
And if they die here you can blame it on me
I've been setting up gravestones in my hometown
Thoughts of particularly old repetition leading to a map aging to the point one lives by the creases rather than actively following any roads is intriguing - at this point in the game it is very distinct that the characters have rotten selective memories and kind of just ghost the lifestyle patterns they used to have, sometimes intentionally. Then we have more talk of 'towns,' the singer wishing a pox upon it, wanting to burn it down, and alluding to mass death (perhaps like the death of Sensei's class, though the details to this (barring a bus plummeting off a cliff) escape me; a favorite idea of mine is that after Sensei commits suicide, each of his class follows in turn because they can't live without his dick, though sadly it is also apparent that his over-sexualized body comes from his self-perception as a sex object rather than being an actual aspect of his true self).
Anyway, although it took longer than I intended, in the above paragraphs I gave examples of lyrics to demonstrate the clear thematic parallels of Good Kid's lyrics to Lessons in Love. It is a rather fitting band for the game, though I will again warn that many of these ideas are 'generic' (though I prefer the terminology 'aesthetically primal.') We could select a totally random band like Valleyheart, comb through lyrics, and point to lines like 'There's a knock on the door of my wavering troubled consciousness / and it's hard to ignore as the weather gets better outside / sure the blooming spring brings a brand new sense of accomplishment / what's the good if it doesn't feel right" or  Take my worn out sense, make it new again / I think I've lost myself, can you heal my head?" However, in the broad scheme, I feel comfortable imagining the resonance He may have felt listening to good kid and the ideas He may have had when putting in the game, so claims that the songs are totally out of place seem disagreeable to me. Even were I not to like the songs, they give much food for contemplation and - to me - tie certain thematic knots in certain points of the long, long string that is The Game.
But is it not by lyrics that songs are most often judged; there is a strong tendency to simply absorb the sounds and then either smile or frown, with the former being a stamp of approval and the latter being a judgement of failure. This is another topic worthy of its own discussion: there is a STRONG tendency in critics to brutally tear apart a piece of media's story, visuals, etc, but completely throw their hands up at the music and say 'eh well I don't know about music so I can't say much but I like it / dislike it?'. This has perturbed me for a long time since it is so ubiquitous. I think there is a sort of mysticism to our resonance with air vibrations that compel even the most rational of analysis to mentally capitulate to magic and admit defeat. And arguably, this is wise of them, for rational critiques of music as produced by trained musicians are often bemusing - a friend of mine, for example, identifies the IV V iii vi chord progression with razor focus and cries on demand upon hearing it. That is a true story. However, it is hard to say a general audience will nod along and say 'Ah yes, this track was superb due to it's execution of the IV V iii vi chord progression.' In some saddening ways music is a firm bastion that continues to slay the ascent of Objective Critique.
I am no exception here. Not only am I not a musician, but I actively strive to avoid music theory in order to prevent myself from thinking in these concrete terms upon hearing music. Ignorance in this case may be bliss and if I open this Pandora's box it will be when I have exhausted more interesting topics. Nonetheless, I can say that Good Kid's tracks are pleasing to the ear and I found them enjoyable to listen to throughout the course of the Lessons in Love update. (I ESPECIALLY liked the chiptune versions present in Sensei Quest and left the game open for days at a time to listen to them before I realized that He had not arranged them himself and in fact I could just find them on youtube.) The problem is that this is lacking in substance to note; I may as well describe the strength of orgasmic bliss that rushed through my head as I ejaculated to a specific H-scene (answer: none. I have not whacked the mole to Lessons in Love a single time (nor did I discover it through h-scene tags) which makes me immune to approximately two/thirds of the fourth wall breaks.)
So instead I will try to scrape up a modicum of meaningful analysis. After hours of contemplation (again, listening to Bubbly - Good Kid) I have forged the shaky but perhaps meaningful idea that the Good Kid tracks provide valuable contrast. Ah, contrast, what a word beloved by critics and analysts alike! Let us ignore the desiccated skin of an overused term to instead identify what this means. After hundreds of hours of primarily ambient background tracks dotted by more contemplative, emotional tracks and distorted mockeries of them we are blasted with full-on upbeat indie rock so popular by the Youth that it is well-known for being officially included in the literal game Fortnite (to say nothing of the name of the band being literally Good Kid).
One does not be an analyst to notice this huge tonal whiplash. Indeed, it is this whiplash which has earned much ire! I saw one comment from someone aghast that after LiL consistently picked so many fitting, emotional tracks, the Good Kid update suddenly blew that all up will ill-fitting western music. But dare I say... that was the point? Okay, that is venturing too close to Happy Event apologism, so let me explain a bit. It's not like "being bad was the point." It's more like: what's going on at this moment? The class are performing a dorm war without Sensei. For a period they detach themselves from drama and are away from their depressive teacher. In the prime of their seething youth they engage in jubilant festivities and truly throw themselves at simply Having Fun, not to get in their teacher's pants, but to Have Fun - (indeed, those after the dildo take their leave). I would say this moment is so unique in LiL's history such a paradigm shift in music is more than fitting. It arouses excitement and energy in the class as much as us (keep in mind the music is wholly diegetic).
Consider an alternate reality where the dormitory war had a good - let's say great, even - ambient upbeat track to it. Some kind of vocal-free track not unlike ULTRA MEGA BATTLE THEME. This would have a pretty transformative effect; it's unlikely that the moment would have felt different or special, and it would run the risk of feeling more of the same, which would have likely been worse or less meaningful. Of course, we can only theorize at what other tracks may have been used, and I don't mean to say Good Kid was objectively the best choice. However, what I want to highlight is Lessons in Love is a game that is evolving and changing before our eyes, each new chapter a step into a new world. A bucket of cold water like Good Kid being splashed in our faces is precisely the kind of wake up call that a new paradigm calls for. Even those displeased by the reverberations are liable to remember it for months or years to come - and that, I find, is quite an artistic accomplishment.
Anyway, I think that's about all I have to say on this subject for now. The reaction to the Good Kid tracks continues to be as fascinating to me as the tracks themselves. Much like a mine rich in valuable ore, the more I contemplate it the more insight I seem to derive. I think those displeased by the Good Kid tracks may stand to benefit from spending 15 to 20 hours playing Good Kid's EP on loop while paying close attention to the lyrics and attempting to reach their inner child on Field Day. For now, I must give Good Kid EP 3 another listen since I've been biasing 1 and 4 lately. Its track Madeleine is rather interesting itself...
