But in these moments I am far from despondent myself: if Good Kid man never sleeps and never eats, why should I feel bad about it myself? It makes me feel enthused to continue existing, and I give my usual silent prayer of gratitude to Lessons in Love for introducing me to a life-defining band.

But invariably there will come a momentum of contemplation which interrupts the stillness, and in this case it's the community's overall poor reception to the Good Kid tracks. I have nothing bad to say about this in itself - I know one individual who loathes all music with comprehensible lyrics simply because he prefers the more primal enchantment of raw beats to thinking about any such poetry, and I can imagine that the erudite readers of Lessons in Love would have respectably eclectic tastes of their own. However I must say that the sheer vitriol directed at the update and music continue to perplex me to a degree, for while I played the tracks felt completely natural to me, and I found the music fairly good as well. If I had a complaint it was mainly that I felt, in retrospect, it was deceptive for Him to comment on this update having "the most new music on any update since such-and-such" which swelled anticipation for something much more original or unique than a series of Good Kid tracks.

Nonetheless, when reality does not meet your expectation that means one must "update their priors" as we Bayesians say, and I have done so, though my intention here is not to get into that too much. The unique playstyles individuals have go far beyond what can be covered in a brief F95 post - the psychology to vetting all music in a game's updates and deleting tracks which does not suit one's taste, for example, is worthy of a dedicated post. Instead, I thought - as good kid man sings into my ears 'I get the feeling I will someday die, and I'm not going to care' - that it might be fun to record some meditations on the inclusion of Good Kid in Lessons in Love.

The first observation I wish to note is the intriguing fact that Good Kid has official chiptune renditions of their tracks, which were later used in SENSEI QUEST (TM) as we all know. This is intriguing because with a flash of intuition it struck me that Good Kid's tracks in the previous Dorm Wars may have been chosen purely due to the existence of these chiptune tracks. We can imagine that the broad strokes of Sensei Quest being painted years ahead of time (perhaps as early as Dear You was written, though I would have wagered it gestating in His mind since a viewing of Oretachi ni Tsubasa wa Nai, had He seen it), and the moment the good kid chiptune tracks were released the idea snapping into place (them being released, to my knowledge, months after the launch of my game; We have noticed a tendency for Him to track all new releases of relevant artists, so perhaps He saw them as soon as they were uploaded, or perhaps He saw them only later). In any case, speculation of this nature is wholly meaningless as creative inspiration is like - as my Dear Beloved David Lynch would say - like catching a fish from the dark shadows of the mind. It can happen at any time, it is out of one's control, and all one can do is quickly write down the intuitions. Remember to write down your intuitions! The dark energies of the brain are beyond our control, and as the electricity surges all can be gained or lost.

The second observation is of more concrete meaning. Good Kid's lyrics are shockingly well-suited for Lessons in Love's themes. Now, this is something tricky, because I have over time found LiL's themes to be so fundamentally and universally relevant that they can be seen everywhere. For example, I recently watched Arawakawa Under the Bridge to see if perhaps the Arakawa family name was inspired by it, and while at first I was stricken by how perhaps such-and-such denpa was inspired by such-and-such idea, it later became extremely apparent to me that Arakawa is chiefly from Arakawa Naoshi, and BOY, if you want to see the inspiration for ideas, do I recommend watching Your Lie In April! HA HA HA!

That's a tangent though - the reality is that such primal themes such as mental illness, the seasons, etc, are universal to the primal human zeitgeist, and so phantoms of their presence can be seen anywhere. One must be wary of drawing lines between dots which ultimately form a grotesque creature rather than a divine symmetrical shape. However, in LiL's case, it's a fact Good Kid tracks were put into the game, and thus are worthy of special attention. To that end I have selected three tracks for our lyrical analysis: Summer, Second Rate Town, and Pox. I have implied analysis of Bubbly above - I trust the reader to determine the significance of staying inside all the time and having a lack of care for death.

Firstly, "Summer" should draw attention for its name alone, for of all the seasons we can say that Summer has presently been "The most important" in Lessons in Love in certain senses. Let us look at some choice lyrics:

I thought the world ended in March
Until I heard the doorbell ring
Can’t keep from falling apart
But I’ll glue back everything again

This can’t be the end
This can’t be the end
This can’t be the end
This can’t be the end
Of all that summer had to say
What little time has gone away

Much like killing frogs and jokes by dissecting them, I am wary about placing definitive interpretations for lyrics. Even if the lyricist were to have a specific idea in mind, it's important that art takes a life on its own and new meaning can be derived through different ways of looking at it. Thus what I offer here is only one interpretation which ideally would be used for fuel as future thought.

As made more clear in a post by the band, this is a song about picking up the pieces of yourself after you've fallen apart and accepting your flaws - including the parts of yourself you don't love. If one did not immediately recoil in realization as they draw a parallel from that to SeleGHAghaCOUGH COUGH from that to Sensei then I am uncertain what to say. The cycle of being unable to believe something is over (in this case: summer, perhaps his Hot Boy Summer, his time of turning around and having the happiest times with his students), to being determined to "piece yourself back together" to try again, etc, are all potently relevant to Lessons in Love. The song even references the wings of a sparrow - what this means honestly I don't know but it's a bird so you know has to be pretty potent. I could go on but we have two more tracks to glance at. (I recommend watching the music video for Summer; it honestly helps a lot with interpreting the lyrics).

The second track is 'Second Rate Town.' Now this one is a jam. Let's get right to the lyrics.


This is a first rate town
But all you ever notice are the ways it’s stretched too far
And it has been knocked down
Well some of us are still left here between the scars
When you look around all you ever notice is you cannot see the stars
This is a first rate town a first rate town you know
You just can’t see very far


Well it will fade as all things must
I loved you but you didn’t love me enough
Winter comes, the car will rust
I’ll start it up then always run a little rough

Obviously, my mind here is drawn to Kumonoami. One could certainly say that the town is stretched way too thin, and that Sensei is noticing it, though perhaps the more interesting aspect is the way in which the singer seems to be pleading with an individual to like a place more than they do - this song actually has two different titles, First-Rate Town and Second-Rate Town. Well, which is it? It's ambiguous, just like how Kumonoami is ambiguously a based town or not. You have certain individuals pleading with Sensei to love it there, while he may at times hate it there. Of particular interest is the background line "You can never leave," implying being trapped. Then there is "it will fade as all things must, I loved you but you didn't love me enough," which makes me think of either Sensei's trauma for Maya's suicide fading, OR Maya identifying that Sensei (as revealed by him choosing to abandon her when she got pregnant) didn't love her as much as she loved him. These are just tenuous connections, though, and not the purpose of the song. Nevertheless it's enjoyable to imagine this as a Kumonoami theme song of sorts. Of the songs played in LiL this one stuck out to me the most in the moment due to this.

The third track is 'Pox.' I chose this one purely because someone I know disliked all the Good Kid tracks, but said 'Pox' was the exception and the only one they liked. This may as well be random selection and will help prevent cherry picking in this analysis. I will now take a look to see what meaning I may derive.


My ancestral passage here
Was written down each year by year
But the map is too old, see they’ve forgotten the roads
And so we're living by the creases.

A pox, a pox, upon this town
I'd give it up just to burn it down
And if they die here you can blame it on me
I've been setting up gravestones in my hometown


Thoughts of particularly old repetition leading to a map aging to the point one lives by the creases rather than actively following any roads is intriguing - at this point in the game it is very distinct that the characters have rotten selective memories and kind of just ghost the lifestyle patterns they used to have, sometimes intentionally. Then we have more talk of 'towns,' the singer wishing a pox upon it, wanting to burn it down, and alluding to mass death (perhaps like the death of Sensei's class, though the details to this (barring a bus plummeting off a cliff) escape me; a favorite idea of mine is that after Sensei commits suicide, each of his class follows in turn because they can't live without his dick, though sadly it is also apparent that his over-sexualized body comes from his self-perception as a sex object rather than being an actual aspect of his true self).

Anyway, although it took longer than I intended, in the above paragraphs I gave examples of lyrics to demonstrate the clear thematic parallels of Good Kid's lyrics to Lessons in Love. It is a rather fitting band for the game, though I will again warn that many of these ideas are 'generic' (though I prefer the terminology 'aesthetically primal.') We could select a totally random band like Valleyheart, comb through lyrics, and point to lines like 'There's a knock on the door of my wavering troubled consciousness / and it's hard to ignore as the weather gets better outside / sure the blooming spring brings a brand new sense of accomplishment / what's the good if it doesn't feel right" or Take my worn out sense, make it new again / I think I've lost myself, can you heal my head?" However, in the broad scheme, I feel comfortable imagining the resonance He may have felt listening to good kid and the ideas He may have had when putting in the game, so claims that the songs are totally out of place seem disagreeable to me. Even were I not to like the songs, they give much food for contemplation and - to me - tie certain thematic knots in certain points of the long, long string that is The Game.

But is it not by lyrics that songs are most often judged; there is a strong tendency to simply absorb the sounds and then either smile or frown, with the former being a stamp of approval and the latter being a judgement of failure. This is another topic worthy of its own discussion: there is a STRONG tendency in critics to brutally tear apart a piece of media's story, visuals, etc, but completely throw their hands up at the music and say 'eh well I don't know about music so I can't say much but I like it / dislike it?'. This has perturbed me for a long time since it is so ubiquitous. I think there is a sort of mysticism to our resonance with air vibrations that compel even the most rational of analysis to mentally capitulate to magic and admit defeat. And arguably, this is wise of them, for rational critiques of music as produced by trained musicians are often bemusing - a friend of mine, for example, identifies the IV V iii vi chord progression with razor focus and cries on demand upon hearing it. That is a true story. However, it is hard to say a general audience will nod along and say 'Ah yes, this track was superb due to it's execution of the IV V iii vi chord progression.' In some saddening ways music is a firm bastion that continues to slay the ascent of Objective Critique.

I am no exception here. Not only am I not a musician, but I actively strive to avoid music theory in order to prevent myself from thinking in these concrete terms upon hearing music. Ignorance in this case may be bliss and if I open this Pandora's box it will be when I have exhausted more interesting topics. Nonetheless, I can say that Good Kid's tracks are pleasing to the ear and I found them enjoyable to listen to throughout the course of the Lessons in Love update. (I ESPECIALLY liked the chiptune versions present in Sensei Quest and left the game open for days at a time to listen to them before I realized that He had not arranged them himself and in fact I could just find them on youtube.) The problem is that this is lacking in substance to note; I may as well describe the strength of orgasmic bliss that rushed through my head as I ejaculated to a specific H-scene (answer: none. I have not whacked the mole to Lessons in Love a single time (nor did I discover it through h-scene tags) which makes me immune to approximately two/thirds of the fourth wall breaks.)

So instead I will try to scrape up a modicum of meaningful analysis. After hours of contemplation (again, listening to Bubbly - Good Kid) I have forged the shaky but perhaps meaningful idea that the Good Kid tracks provide valuable contrast. Ah, contrast, what a word beloved by critics and analysts alike! Let us ignore the desiccated skin of an overused term to instead identify what this means. After hundreds of hours of primarily ambient background tracks dotted by more contemplative, emotional tracks and distorted mockeries of them we are blasted with full-on upbeat indie rock so popular by the Youth that it is well-known for being officially included in the literal game Fortnite (to say nothing of the name of the band being literally Good Kid).

One does not be an analyst to notice this huge tonal whiplash. Indeed, it is this whiplash which has earned much ire! I saw one comment from someone aghast that after LiL consistently picked so many fitting, emotional tracks, the Good Kid update suddenly blew that all up will ill-fitting western music. But dare I say... that was the point? Okay, that is venturing too close to Happy Event apologism, so let me explain a bit. It's not like "being bad was the point." It's more like: what's going on at this moment? The class are performing a dorm war without Sensei. For a period they detach themselves from drama and are away from their depressive teacher. In the prime of their seething youth they engage in jubilant festivities and truly throw themselves at simply Having Fun, not to get in their teacher's pants, but to Have Fun - (indeed, those after the dildo take their leave). I would say this moment is so unique in LiL's history such a paradigm shift in music is more than fitting. It arouses excitement and energy in the class as much as us (keep in mind the music is wholly diegetic).

Consider an alternate reality where the dormitory war had a good - let's say great, even - ambient upbeat track to it. Some kind of vocal-free track not unlike ULTRA MEGA BATTLE THEME. This would have a pretty transformative effect; it's unlikely that the moment would have felt different or special, and it would run the risk of feeling more of the same, which would have likely been worse or less meaningful. Of course, we can only theorize at what other tracks may have been used, and I don't mean to say Good Kid was objectively the best choice. However, what I want to highlight is Lessons in Love is a game that is evolving and changing before our eyes, each new chapter a step into a new world. A bucket of cold water like Good Kid being splashed in our faces is precisely the kind of wake up call that a new paradigm calls for. Even those displeased by the reverberations are liable to remember it for months or years to come - and that, I find, is quite an artistic accomplishment.

Anyway, I think that's about all I have to say on this subject for now. The reaction to the Good Kid tracks continues to be as fascinating to me as the tracks themselves. Much like a mine rich in valuable ore, the more I contemplate it the more insight I seem to derive. I think those displeased by the Good Kid tracks may stand to benefit from spending 15 to 20 hours playing Good Kid's EP on loop while paying close attention to the lyrics and attempting to reach their inner child on Field Day. For now, I must give Good Kid EP 3 another listen since I've been biasing 1 and 4 lately. Its track Madeleine is rather interesting itself...


The sun had shined, the earth as well
Her eyes were two half moons
And even when we lost ourselves
To something in between
The words we shared are all still there
To show us where we'd been

I'll go wherever you go
I'll go wherever you go
I'll go wherever you go
I'll go wherever you go

I saw one comment from someone aghast that after LiL consistently picked so many fitting, emotional tracks, the Good Kid update suddenly blew that all up will ill-fitting western music. But dare I say... that was the point? Okay, that is venturing too close to Happy Event apologism, so let me explain a bit. It's not like "being bad was the point." It's more like: what's going on at this moment? The class are performing a dorm war without Sensei. For a period they detach themselves from drama and are away from their depressive teacher. In the prime of their seething youth they engage in jubilant festivities and truly throw themselves at simply Having Fun, not to get in their teacher's pants, but to Have Fun - (indeed, those after the dildo take their leave). I would say this moment is so unique in LiL's history such a paradigm shift in music is more than fitting. It arouses excitement and energy in the class as much as us (keep in mind the music is wholly diegetic).
Consider an alternate reality where the dormitory war had a good - let's say great, even - ambient upbeat track to it. Some kind of vocal-free track not unlike ULTRA MEGA BATTLE THEME. This would have a pretty transformative effect; it's unlikely that the moment would have felt different or special, and it would run the risk of feeling more of the same, which would have likely been worse or less meaningful. Of course, we can only theorize at what other tracks may have been used, and I don't mean to say Good Kid was objectively the best choice. However, what I want to highlight is Lessons in Love is a game that is evolving and changing before our eyes, each new chapter a step into a new world. A bucket of cold water like Good Kid being splashed in our faces is precisely the kind of wake up call that a new paradigm calls for. Even those displeased by the reverberations are liable to remember it for months or years to come - and that, I find, is quite an artistic accomplishment.
Anyway, I think that's about all I have to say on this subject for now. The reaction to the Good Kid tracks continues to be as fascinating to me as the tracks themselves. Much like a mine rich in valuable ore, the more I contemplate it the more insight I seem to derive. I think those displeased by the Good Kid tracks may stand to benefit from spending 15 to 20 hours playing Good Kid's EP on loop while paying close attention to the lyrics and attempting to reach their inner child on Field Day. For now, I must give Good Kid EP 3 another listen since I've been biasing 1 and 4 lately. Its track Madeleine is rather interesting itself...

With all the replaying going on, I began working on a save from the end of v30 so I could go through the Amy Happy Event. I found something that appears to be foreshadowing that I am not sure anyone picked up (did a thread search and came up empty).

The first v32 character event I played was Io's Tennis Ball, where Akira spends most of the event in the water at the bath house, trying to coax Io into the bath with him before she has to leave to help a customer. Sekai appears, Akira almost drowns, Io saves him and drags him up to her room.

After he regains consciousness, this is his internal monologue...










Didn't notice it before but it jumped out at me this time, Akira sick to his stomach for what he has been trying to do to Io, well before Io's Stomachache event.

Nothing brilliant or lore-busting, but surprised I didn't pick up on it before nor did I see any other mentions of this during a couple thread searches.

That's very generous of you. I've been trying to raise the quality of my posts precisely to win over kind folks such as yourself and rebuild my shattered reputation in my home-away-from-home here. It doesn't seem to be working so well though... the Ignore wall is a harsh one, and those who choose to shelter themselves so are certainly beyond the reach of frail hands such as these. But putting them aside I am at a loss. Although aiming for smaller, snippy posts would certainly have a greater response in the divine social media algorithm, those are the kind of posts I could make on another account. When it comes to this being I need to speak with its particular purpose and thus speak at length. A lot of words means I have a lot to say on the matter, but it seems length is consistently rejected... I don't understand accusations of pretention because I don't know what that means. To attempt to affect greater importance than I have is beyond me when I am uncertain of any importance of my own. What am I to do? I am sad and lost, but cannot bring myself to silence the voice dictating what to write. In the end, I may end up having to scream into the void, for ten-odd years, waiting for someone who will listen without hiding awkwardly within the crowd. I've spent enough time talking to plants already, but I can do more. Perhaps a tl;dr will help after all though I don't like them too much myself since numerical scores and summaries tend to draw engagement from those who skip the rest to read the conclusion despite the elaboration being more important than the conclusion, like showing your work on a math problem...

Regardless if that is true or not, Akira is still trapped in his relationship with Sekai. He never left.

So that's the big issue. He can still act on instinct (lust), and recognize that some things are wrong (often things that were done to him aka things against one's will). But that's the measure of it, as a shadow there's not much that he can do, especially changing.

"Stomachache" and the one event with him showering Chinami (in which she straight up addresses his pedophilia so well that many think that was Himawari). Will that eventually make a difference as to Akira's end between green and red path? It remains to be seen.

Weird... funny, but definitely weird... and i kinda don't like it for her, it undermines her characterization, Chinami is pretty damn smart, very observant and good at poking at things until they reveal themselves... that scene was very her, we know she only speaks in 3rd person for Chika's benefit, she just wants to understand the problem that caused the fight so she can help her sister, figuring out Akira is a pedo was a side product of that. If it was just Himawari... wtf was the point of any of that?
Click to expand...
I agree. It definitely wasn’t Himawari. People are too quick to jump to that conclusion sometimes.

Look at the events “Holden Caulfield”
(Chinami event) and “Rivals (Taco Tuesday)” (Noriko event). Particularly at the flashbacks with Wizard Maya and Noriko.

They way they speak in those flashbacks do not fit their age. Like… at all. It’s almost like their mannerisms didn’t change from past to present.

With that in mind, it isn’t too far fetched to conclude that Chinami is the same way.

She’s been holed up in her home for years, watched mature shows on TV like Game of Thrones, and got recent access to the internet when she got her new phone. No duh she’s gonna learn about some non-Wizard friendly topics.

And just to parrot it a second time: Chinami is stuck at home. What else can she do for entertainment when she’s by herself?

With all that free time comes boredom. With boredom comes curiosity. With curiosity comes interest. With interest comes learning. And with learning comes knowledge.

As Bingoogus said, Chinami is a smart and perceptive girl; something that has been alluded to for multiple chapters now. This isn’t new.

Tl;dr - Not Himawari. Is actually Chinami.

With every interaction, you can visually see Makoto's innocence being stripped away, which is weird considering she works at a porn shop.

I'm trying to figure out if there is a pattern to the static. I feel like there is but... what? It's at the tip of the tongue... or brain, more like. I'm thinking of like a mix of unexpected and some kind of mental disorder and anomaly. Like something that isn't suppose to happen. Some consequence of the reincarnation.
Hmm. You know, I wonder if there is a connection between the mc is a bad person, this is not a porn game but rather a game with porn and this weird phenomena. I have nothing conclusive figured out yet but it gets me thinking. Maybe I'm being too pessimistic as even real life can have that happy sweet ending and that might equate to an actual sweet sex scene without the static interfering. Now that I'm convinced Yumi is a tsundere, I know she haven't reported him yet because he haven't overstepped her current boundaries and she loves the attention. Of course the mc doesn't know that and I probably wouldn't have either if I didn't pay specific attention and got tipped of to the likelihood and process of elimination, part in thanks to Maya.

The game sure likes to put random hexdecimal secrets every here and there. Chika's phone says "hope" when translated. Why? Can't tell if that's a rhetorical question or not.

Well that's a weird way to introduce a new character.
What... the fuck just happened? This "anywhere at all" Sana event is odd.

Wires mentioned, alarms blaring in my head. Probably false alarm but y'all seem obsessed with them so.

You just know neither of the four needed that discount. Ayane could probably pay for all of it no problem, yet they had to attempt this.

This something absolutely hilarious about a smug Ayane trying to feed a furious Maya. The craziest part is that it's actually working, wtf?

The illusion of choice in this Yumi scene.
Well... this somewhat fucked up scene proves that he is not in control of his body, she is not strong and can cry. They are both victims of whatever appears to be wrong with his body.
This scenes makes me feel kinda bad...
Is this what it would feel like to lose control and do something you will regret for the rest of your life?
Is THIS what they mean by "it's hard to tell what is real and not"? "None of this ever happened!"
I think the only thing that event served to do is enabled my protective instinct of her or something.

AGH, fuck! I let my guard down and now I get jump scared during Ayane's dojo event. Really goes to show that they can strike whenever and wherever and I am not in control of that what so ever. Like yeah, I did get just a slight warning when he started talking about something that could be seen as forbidden knowledge but still.

Finally a proper introduction to this Molly figure.

Am I weird for thinking Ayane is a keeper? Someone out there is probably saying "he has no idea..." or "clueless". That remains to be seen.

I think it says a lot about a person by how good they are at taking care of someone sick. This is pretty sweet, even tho it is a little rough given the mc's track record.

Yeah, Miku is officially the densest girl when it comes to sexual stuff.

HOLY FUCK! That's like a fucking cannonball being fired! Out of all the things that would spook me...

...here we go again.
Oh fuck... and that binary translates to a continuous string of "get away get away get away". Honestly, I should have expected this dark closed storage locker to turn into something creepy.

Oh fuck that... Give me back my F tier tomboy. I want nothing to do with... whatever the fuck that is. You know I don't know what the hell happy events are going to be if these normal events can be like this.
Wait... What if Miku's trauma involves a gunshot or loud slamming?
Oh come on... I would like to say I'm getting tired of being startled, but I feel like this is still just the beginning.
Well, that just happened.

Welp, that's it for today.

posts.content_html_raw:
Moonflare said:
I have said this before but Akira can't do anything before he figures out his deal with Sekai. I had a girlfriend explain this to me once, that some people are so lost in their own hell that all they can do is bring others into hell as well (often not even aware that they're doing it).

Regardless if that is true or not, Akira is still trapped in his relationship with Sekai. He doesn't want to have children, he doesn't want to get married, he doesn't want to have a life, he doesn't want to live because there's no real Akira here - Akira is still in that moment of seeing the car tumbling around. He never left.

So that's the big issue. He can still act on instinct (lust), and recognize that some things are wrong (often things that were done to him aka things against one's will). But that's the measure of it, as a shadow there's not much that he can do, especially changing.

In fact, I think the Akira that ended up marrying Sekai didn't solve his issues either. But that's a hunch, there's not enough to go around. It's just a feeling I have.

Now, what's interesting to me, that's also been talked about before is that he mainly deals with these issues on the green path. "Stomachache" and the one event with him showering Chinami (in which she straight up addresses his pedophilia so well that many think that was Himawari). Will that eventually make a difference as to Akira's end between green and red path? It remains to be seen.
Click to expand...
It hasn't been touched upon much yet, but Sensei's/Akira's issues probably even predate Sekai.

Apparently, Sensei's mother didn't like him:
Yasu - "His mother's name was Saki..."
- "She didn't like him very much."
Saki - 'It's Upside Down" (Backwards, Upside Down, and weird.)
(Chapter 3 'The Cracking of the Egg (Nothing is Beautiful)' Main Event)
And he seems to block her out even more than Sekai. Considering the Sky background, Religious, and Upside Down connections, his Mother might be far more important than has been revealed.

Putting a few implications together, I wouldn't be too surprised if she violated him due to him reminding her of his father, who may have left her for/cheated on her with Sekai's mother, Miu.

Not to mention; Ami talks about grandma at times like she's notable (and somewhat acts like her). Albeit, recent revelations could suggest she's referring to Miu instead of Saki, but I doubt it due to the religious connection. Miu's most defining trait was probably being scared of everything to the point that she's thrown up at school.

Saki was peculiar even back in the previous game, 'Nothing is Beautiful':
Saki, Child of God (backwards) - "How does it feel?"
With the hands being cut off thing that gets mentioned at times, seemingly starting from her:
Yuu Narrator - "She will cut my hands off."
- "It has happened before."
Plus the Whales, Religious stuff, and Plants, etc, references, also seem to come from her.

Overall: Sensei's issues probably predate Sekai, with her just being more prominent now that he's finally acknowledging her.

Of course, there's also the potential mental illness that seems inherited from Sensei's/Akira's father, on top of this, but Saki may have been his first abuser. Then there's his problems with Nozomu, and Sekai. Then there's the Maya stuff, and whatever else.
-----
Now, to wait for his Niki problems once she pulls a Sekai from Sensei's perspective.

Both have gave him their word that they'd never leave him:

Vs:

Sensei - "Will you really never leave me?"
Sekai - "I don't think I'd be able to if I tried."
(Chapter 4 'Kyoto' Happy Event)

Sensei - "Will you really never leave me?"
Niki - "I don't think I'd be able to if I tried."
(Chapter 3 Niki 'How To Make Love Stay' Event)
Of course, we know how things turned out for Sekai:
Sensei - "I'm saying you should leave. You're good at that, aren't you?"
Sekai - "Now I'm just confused. You want me to leave, but you're sad that I'm gone?"
Sensei - "I'm not sad! I'm fine! I've been great since you've left!"
(Chapter 3 'Girls Just Want to Have Fun' Main Event)

If he loses Niki (if she "leaves"), well, I don't see how Sensei could recover from that. Especially if he's...involved:
Sensei (mentally unstable) - "I will not let another girl die."
(Chapter 3 'Party Animal' Main Event)

Also, come on Niki, you surely know what Death Flags are:
Niki - "No matter what you've done or what you'll do, I'll be right there with you."
(Chapter 3 Niki 'The End of the Tour (Glasswalker)' Event)

- "You'd have to get rid of me by force. I'd never leave on my own."
(Chapter 3 Niki 'How To Make Love Stay' Event)
R.I.P.

posts.content_html_raw:
Day 4 of playing. Character count: 7129(these are probably meaningless but you know roughly how much you are about to read and it will help me calculate the final score int he future). Surprisingly I didn't get to trigger yesterdays happy event.
Starting off good with that innuendos "You can do me whenever you want, Chika"

She does look beautiful in that dress.

So that's called a kabedon. I've heard that word before but never connected the dots.

Omg, there is so much romantic tension in this Chika scene right now, the freaking cheek hold! A simple gesture but a good one nonetheless.
OHHHKEY and she's nibbling his thumb! Yep, straight to top tier with her.

Yumi being easily spooked by horror movies? I gotta see that!

But that... never happened? The kiss with Yumi...
Unless I've entered some section where there's a side event branch that never actually happens but tells a disturbing story.
And honestly yeah, thinking about an action and doing it are so tremendously different.
If you can sense a person's self control, mind reading would be much less scary.
I... see. So that did happen and the smilie just basically means no and means yes. Simple enough. I honestly expected more to happen tho. Mc never did find out what her secret was or at least the player didn't.

No fucking way, 2 happy events yet to be triggered... Well it kinda looks like Maya has two happy events or more. Guess I will find out.

It just occurred to me that Maya might actually be a kuudere. Or am I wrong to make that assumption?

Haruka's entry added. I guess it needs to be more... official for the characters to be added.

It's a little unexpected. I went to sleep last night right after Miku's happy event appeared. Just earlier, another Maya happy event appeared and was triggered pretty quickly. Just goes to show that autovn works in mysterious ways.
Welp... here we go again.

Surprisingly I have very little to say about this scene.
The only thing I gathered from that and the previous happy event is that Maya is either very sexually active or have past sexual trauma, or both. If that is the message the dev wants to send then you succeeded, if it's not, then what am I suppose to make of this?
It did nothing to change my opinion of her because these happy events are not... real. Also starting to think the affection score does not follow a logical pattern and may increase regardless if the events are real or not. Or the player sees a warped event of what actually happens.
Hmm, now that I think about it. If my theory about Maya having past sexual trauma is true, it would also explain why she doesn't like or trust the mc and more so since he doesn't belong in that body.

Wait... huh? Too young to get an ID? You know what, nevermind.

Honestly, I'm not really surprised Rin is lesbian. Question is if she's only lesbian or actually bi. There are so many girls in this game that it without really matter if one or two of them turned out to be lesbian only.
That would be interesting now that I think about it. She's being the wingwoman, so why not explore a game where you help the wingwoman find someone who likes her?

That's a mouthful. Mildly creepy huh? Well, Makoto does look good in that swimsuit.

Oh, I see. A little girl with asthma and a compromised immune system. That's pretty rough yeah. But I think the implication that Yumi is taking care of this one occasionally puts her in a new light.
She's a precious one. Makes me wonder tho. Why is it that I dislike children irl but not in games? This protective instinct, cuteness overload. Maybe it's because a child in a game won't do anything to me personally that I dislike but as children as unpredictable, I tend to keep my distance. I wonder if my reaction to being a father would be kind of like my reaction to fictional children like this one?

My theory so far is that Chinami might remind him of Ami and Ami was likely a similar age when he picked her up. Although there could be something else.

Aww... That's so sad... Man it hurts to see Chika like that.
It's during these moments that the mc acts more human.

Well this is... concerning. His indeed seeing these things happen but no one else is.

WTH? Now I have to worry about the game auto forwarding in some scenes.

I didn't expect that out of all the characters, Makoto would be the first one caught in this compromising position. "sowing the seeds" huh... Interesting.
"Surely, nothing but good will come of this!" Hmm... I dunno about that one. I'm inclined to believe the opposite is the case. But how bad it will get remains to be seen.

His unwilling to use a mop to help Makoto clean a pool but is willing to go jogging with Miku. Do I need to apply the micro reasons to understand how this mc thinks?

Maybe don't pretend to be melting bodies in your room while changing clothes with your door unlocked. That's just asking for trouble.
Mc agrees with me.

All this existentialism talk from Maya just makes me feel like she needs to let go off it. Enjoy life some more and stop being concerned about the infinite cycles of the exact same infinitely rare event.

I expected to find out that a kotatsu was just a table with a built in blanket but then it told me it also has an electric heat source. Huh, expected knowledge. I suppose that's why they are so popular.

I'm surprised that whole "rewind/repeat/refuse" event didn't involve any static. No idea why it didn't. I expected it throughout the whole thing.

That's a lot of hexdecimals... I translated it but it comes out with some gibberish. The part at the end did say something about jerking off. Also it kinda seemed irish or something. I'm sure there is a proper translation of whatever plays in "ode to a marsh warbler".

It's sorta like Maya's first happy event but less disturbing and not officially recognized as a happy event.

Hey now, my eyes are very trustworthy...

Oh great, now even the plants are talking. Just a normal Sunday morning.
What the fuck is even happening right now...?

Wait... Are they going where I think they are?
They are... Ami's parents gravestone. It makes sense why Maya was so insistent on him not hurting her. It kinda makes sense why the body was speaking reflexively, in a "I've been reincarnated into an adult body" sort of way. What doesn't make sense is the whole setup, the confusing nonsense with the talking plant, the angels, the perversion, the bird nonsense. Why? Art. That's probably why. But my mind isn't open to art. At least not to the degree of keeping up with this game I suppose.

When the game really tries to tell you something, the message is so strong. Even if the messages are hidden behind a facade of a cute (not)porn game, the messages are so very strong.

This was... sudden. "Forever yours (top of the world)" or "less like the vulture" the second event title is a bit strange.
In a way what the mc just said seemed right. His not built for love, but if he can help someone else feel it, he will do it again.
Static during insertion? Well I guess the symbolism isn't stopping for anything.
Well, the scenes aren't animated. Or at least this one wasn't. I guess that makes sense for a not porn game. Guess the animated tag is reserved for the static transitions.
Also I think the game is going for the mental sex over the visual kind, which would make sense for a well written story based game.
And a slightly updated (as scuff as always) tierlist. I should probably be following a traditional S-F tier list instead but that's plans for when I meet more girls.


Rin: Nice hair. Surprisingly bland unless Chika is around. Also seem to have a bit of a wingman personality.
Chika: Turns out she's actually really cute and beautiful in a dress.
Kirin and Karin: They were strangely beautiful when I first saw them.
Chinami: So adorable! Must protecc!

Note.

The further top left the character is, the more I like them. But I may sometime sleep on the left to right order.

If the color of the tiles are the same, it means they are equally important.

If I didn't mention someone, I probably don't have anything noteworthy to say yet or they slipped my mind.

Tierlists are hard, so the rankings may not be quite accurate to my true emotions and changes over time.


Unchanged since yesterday.

Yumi: I can't WAIT to see how the story with her escalates. Every time he messed with her, it's so fun and I like her appearance too.
Ami: Red hair, she loves you.
Ayane: Long hair, she loves you.
Chika: I expected an annoying gyaru girl who acts way too popular but I got someone chill and down to earth, fun to be around.
Makoto: I love it when he messes with her. I slightly dislike her appearance and how studious she is.
Sana: Very precious.
Maya: The mystery behind her is intriguing.

Miku: Not into tomboys.
Futaba: Not into wider girls.

That's a lot of hexdecimals... I translated it but it comes out with some gibberish. The part at the end did say something about jerking off. Also it kinda seemed irish or something. I'm sure there is a proper translation of whatever plays in "ode to a marsh warbler".
It's sorta like Maya's first happy event but less disturbing and not officially recognized as a happy event.
Hey now, my eyes are very trustworthy...
Oh great, now even the plants are talking. Just a normal Sunday morning.
What the fuck is even happening right now...?
Wait... Are they going where I think they are?
They are... Ami's parents gravestone. It makes sense why Maya was so insistent on him not hurting her. It kinda makes sense why the body was speaking reflexively, in a "I've been reincarnated into an adult body" sort of way. What doesn't make sense is the whole setup, the confusing nonsense with the talking plant, the angels, the perversion, the bird nonsense. Why? Art. That's probably why. But my mind isn't open to art. At least not to the degree of keeping up with this game I suppose.
When the game really tries to tell you something, the message is so strong. Even if the messages are hidden behind a facade of a cute (not)porn game, the messages are so very strong.
This was... sudden. "Forever yours (top of the world)" or "less like the vulture" the second event title is a bit strange.
In a way what the mc just said seemed right. His not built for love, but if he can help someone else feel it, he will do it again.
Static during insertion? Well I guess the symbolism isn't stopping for anything.
Well, the scenes aren't animated. Or at least this one wasn't. I guess that makes sense for a not porn game. Guess the animated tag is reserved for the static transitions.
Also I think the game is going for the mental sex over the visual kind, which would make sense for a well written story based game.

The supernatural aspects also likely have affected both girls their whole lives. With their families already being involved in whatever is going on.

Of course, whether any of these characters and their backstories actually existed before the Resets, isn't entirely clear.

Spoiler

Hm, something that I don't think has really came up yet (And where I'm somewhat leaning in the what the hell is going on with Ami stuff):

The idea that versions of the characters could possibly steal the bodies of other versions whenever:
Last update literally had Ayane, Makoto, Maya, likely Nodoka, Sensei, and Yumi all steal the bodies of others versions of themselves, with other lives.
  • Makoto was a virgin in our timeline, but in that one, that Makoto wasn't, during presumably the same time period. Our Makoto in that Makoto's body then had a threesome with that Sekai, and our Sensei in that Sensei's body.
  • Our Nodoka seemingly died in that other Nodoka's body. Two Nodokas may have died. Ours mentally, theirs physically.
  • Our Maya (New Maya), jumped through multiple different Mayas, making out with an Ami in one, two different Senseis in two others, and was sexually abused by an Ami (perhaps the same one she made out with) in another Maya's body. (Edit: Actually kissed 3 different Senseis as 3 different Mayas)
This hasn't been talked about, but was definitely something notable as even Sensei didn't want to fuck another Sensei's Ami, so that when that Sensei returned, his life would be like he had it.

Of course, there's nothing saying that the reverse couldn't or hasn't happened. When the characters "Black Out" or "Time Skip", or "Slip", going on "Auto Pilot", well, who's to say that other versions of them haven't just taken over.

This could also explain the inconsistent memories. Meaning that they aren't all actually inconsistent or false. Some may just be literally different because things happened differently where they were from.
-----

This also begs the question...are any or these girls, currently, actually the same ones from the start? Or simply other versions that have gotten swapped out at one point or another...

I also have to wonder if Happy Ending Ami might know how to steal the lives of other Amis:
Ami - "We get to stay together now. Just you, me, and Daddy for the rest of our lives. And then other lives. Until the egg has finally cracked and there are no more lives to live."
(Chapter 4 'Pop Goes The Weasel' Main Event)
She could be that Psycho Ami, and just knows how to enter other timelines and versions of herself.

I have a feeling we haven't seen the last of her or her family. (I'm considering calling them the "Rabbit Family" based off the 'Arms Bent Back' Happy Event)

Hell, we might have not even seen the last of this Sensei:
Sensei(?) - "Go on. Scream for help. There's no one around."
- "The list of things I want to do to you would carry on for years."
(Chapter 1 'This Town Has Two Halves' Main Event)
And this may have been what was actually going on when the personalities of other Senseis kept changing from Maya Prime's perspective over the years:
Maya Prime - "But yes. Changes like that are possible. Though they seem to be very rare for anyone but you."
- "You're an entirely different case. You change personalities faster than a girl getting off of a long term relationship changes her hairstyle."
- "I'm surprised you even made it this far as you, to be honest."
- "Do you have any idea how much trouble you've caused me in the past?"
(Chapter 1 'Tradition' Main Event)
Their personality may not have been actually changing. Another Sensei could potentially "slip" into their body, at times, then make it and that world their own. Perhaps without even noticing. Giving off the illusion of a changing personality.

Of course, this is merely speculation for now.

spoilers.title: Day 63-77, some reactions, thoughts and questions
spoilers.html:
Uh oh, drunk Sana... and Sara.
Yeah, it would feel wrong to reject Sara... which is kinda weird considering, well, everything.
Fucking static, NOW what?
Well shit, Sara is quite attractive, huh.
No static on that insertion. I swear, I don't understand the pattern to the static what so ever.

Seems lust events are showing up now.
Replay section has also started appearing for some characters. I wonder if ALL scenes will be there considering autovn don't allow you to interact with the game world. If not, then I'm gonna have to consider grabbing someones save by the time I reach eoc. Regardless I'm gonna have to make a new save myself since I never did check through the computer content to avoid potential spoilers.

If the creepy undertone and the swapping of eye styles weren't there, I would probably easily accept these realistic eyes of Ami's.

Now that is a cursed as fuck sentence "Congratulations! You have fingered your niece!" Gee, thanks, do I get a medal with that too!? Wtf...

You know what I've been struggling with since the start of this game? Remembering Ami's name!!! Why, why do I need to go look into the main girls section just to remember it?

Well now what, did a happy event insta trigger? Yeah. Judging by the emoji it's safe to say it did. And I don't know what the fuck happened to Ayane's face but that thing needs to be buried 7 feet under, because 6 won't be enough to contain it.

Of course Maya is the one who looks normal.
And acts normal in her own not normal way.

I'm so uncomfortably confused by what is happening on my screen!
AAAAA, this is so fucking weird! Cursed sitcoms!

Well, that's not the typical happy event I'm used to.

I have no idea why Sara isn't in the main girls category and that makes me sad.
Honestly, I don't fault Sara for falling for him so easily. He doesn't go out of his way to hurt her, his teaching her daughter, his like... the only male available, his also taking care of a similar age teenager like Sana and his got a big one... yeah.

First it was the Sara "date" then it is a third wheel event, both on the same day. The first one I've encountered so far. Sara seems to somehow be the first with a lot of things.

Why is it strangely attractive that Sara is embarrassed about not being a good cook? He did have that conversation with Futaba about how flaws make you more attractive as long as there's not too many, so that's probably why.

Ami reacting to Sara is fucking hilarious. Like yeah, he wasn't wrong about her freezing, but not in the way I expected. There was no shock just, happy stare.

Sara is dangerously effective at this infiltration thing. The things she does and says are perfect but I somehow struggle to believe she understands exactly how to deal with Ami this early on. She may be hurting the relationship with the mc temporarily but appealing to Amy and her weakpoints is precisely what you have to do. But I imagine it won't be quite so easy with the other girls.

Feel like I've been rambling a lot more today. Maybe I'm just making up for the fact today will be shorter.

In what world is it someone wrong for a girl to climax prematurely? I feel like that's how it's suppose to be.

Wait, Sana is STILL traumatized by the spaghetti incident!? Wait, it's the word!

Just like the mc, I have no intention of playing a game like animal crossing.

Damn, when did Ayane get huge metaphorical balls to stand up to Yumi like this!? Somehow it makes perfect sense for the rich girl to be picking on the delinquent.
Ooo, I saw that slight blush. Honestly, I will take what I can get with Yumi. Just wish autovn could give me some Yumi scenes soon.

GREEEEAT, and now I'm unsettled again. I was just chilling, completely unprepared. Way to ruin the mood. "We're the only two people in the house" "you don't know that."
Honestly that scene could have just been the everything that happened besides the creep image but whatever. I should be used to this by now but I'm not because the game is so darn cute 99% of the time.

Now what? Is that suppose to happen? They turned into a unfinished painting or something.

I expected one of two things to happen with that bathroom scene. Either something creepy as fuck was going to happen, or Ami walks in naked. I guess I'm glad it was the latter.
I also didn't expect this to be the place where they finally did it, jeez... Well I just now realized that this might be mimicking real life in a way. You don't really know when it will happen for the first time.

This game is so quotable, how lovely "Does your dick feel good... inside of your family?..."

No static what so ever throughout this. It's almost like whatever causes it somehow approves of this relationship.

Rin does strike me as the kind of girl that has something seriously wrong about or around her that would reinforce the horror aspect.
I knew that illuminati painting was too suspicious not to have another purpose.
It's interesting that this is happening in the middle of the fucking day(probably) in a friendly cafe that probably has other people around. Just goes to show that the environment also doesn't matter.
I guess Rin is just one of the secretly fucked up types in the school. I mean, I DID see that one spoiler that happens way ahead and the game isn't exactly making it obscure that she's entirely sane.

WAIT A GOD DAMN MINUTE! She was staring at Chika in the dorms! I didn't know she was bi and had a crush on Chika at that point so I brushed it off to her just getting easily lost looking at nothing, sorta like Futaba I guess? But no, now it makes perfect sense. I mean look at her, that's actually kind of adorable now that I look back.

It's stalking to have a folder saved of public images taken by the person whose being stalked? Well that makes perfect sense. I don't see the flaw in that logic what so ever.
On another note, if I were the mc, I would try to see if I can somehow matchmake Rin and Chika. A triangle relationship would come secondary.

3 happy events queued up. Man, I'm gonna run out of those at this rate.

I also just witnessed the game adding 4 affection points for Yumi to trigger the next event. Finally.

When I first started writing these I was in the mindset that I would choose carefully what was worth writing but now I have once again gotten distracted. My apologies to anyone reading less worthwhile text.

Yumi being more friendly than usual.
Ooooookey... I guess the other side of town kiss actually DID happen and the game is full of shit. Yep, it's confirmed. You never really know what does and does not actually happen.

No, I don't see you. Please fuck off, creepy imitation of Maya...

Such typical tsundere behavior. The mc didn't even comment about it.

The letter 'T'. What kind eldritch nightmare am I gonna witness this time?

Man, why does it have to be so dark, silent and ominous? I want my sitcom back.

What's going on with the music during this scene? Does it go forward then backwards twice then forward again while the AI voice repeats every time or something?

Sooner or later I will find out what is buried underneath his feet. Marks my words, I will have answers!

The happy events don't really seem to be getting any worse in terms of scare value.

That is very risky. Sana is just out to make a phone call and they are going at it.

Click to expand...
I think this is a vital lesson in how to interpret reviews on this site. Many reviews will talk down the plot and writing of a game as pretentious or long-winded or the character development, especially in terms of corruption, as too slow.

In most cases, from my experience, this just underlines that the writing is in fact good, that it takes its time to build up characters and to not rush things to conclusions in an effort to produce lewd scenes to appease the angry mob. In that regard, I am glad that Selebus is a stubborn egg that won't let anyone tell him how to do things.

So as a rule of thumb, when you see those kind of key words in a negative review, it often means the reviewer is a hopeless gooner who struggles with big boy words and essentially just wants a slide show of CGs to beat it off to. If you don't identify with that, you can generally safely disregard such opinions.

posts.content_html_raw:
The social incentives for participating in large, public servers are clear but the implicit and explicit tyranny within them is always sickening to my spirit. Lilcord is a pretty fun place with a lot of great people but there remains a disquieting sense of perpetual unease behind every post and exchange. Everyone knows (though many ignore) that they are being watched and comprehended. That's a distinction few appreciate; being watched is one thing, there's always eyes on everyone, but being COMPREHENDED? That is another story entirely. Consider making an error of some kind, like maybe you bump into an old man on the street, or maybe you tell an impulsive lie to get out of an awkward situation. Simply having some random passersby see this occur is hardly meaningful. They have no thoughts; their heads are empty, the world 'thinks far less of you than you imagine it does' (quote DFW). But image someone in the crowd comprehending - watching on with unblinking, sharp eyes and parsing what they have seen. If you catch their gaze their eyes will bore holes into yours as they deem you a liar, a sinner, one to whom they will REMEMBER as having committed these acts now prescribed to your being in all their significance. IT does NOT become water under the bridge, it becomes sludge coursing through your veins forever, a burden to forever bear, it is a PART OF YOU.

Recall the beaten-down apology of Mr. D after he was muted in Lilcord for X hours after making a joke of ill taste. Recall how he hunched his shoulders and whimpered obsequiously upon his return. Recall the uncomfortable silence and confusion which met him. Recall how his tone henceforth was just a bit more hesitant, a bit more restrained, a bit more scared. His deed was COMPREHENDED. His deed was JUDGED. His deed was REMEMBERED. And Mr. D's veins would not again be free of the sludge of his own filthy sin as long as those eyes remained on him. It should come as no surprise whatsoever what came next for him, though that's a story we all know. And it is why I, myself, cannot bear to resign myself to any such judgment. Should I offer myself up to the judgment of someone let it be my brother or my mother, not some damned another!

The interesting part of this situation, though, and something REALLY interesting, is the psychology of those who observe and comprehend. That is to say the opposite of those who shy their eyes and still their thoughts. Because I think a quirk of observers is the paranoia it induces in themselves. The thought process is something like - "I am observing others, so others may be observing me." This is something that suits Sensei from lessons in love quite well I think. One of the most tell-tale signs of an Observer, someone enacting their own judgment at all times, is that they begin to imagine others are Judging them too. And they know the terror well. So, hilariously, they develop this tendency to respond almost exclusively to negative feedback - a compulsive urge to address all criticism. Positive feedback is almost irrelevant; perhaps it surges the ego for a moment, but never for long, so they understand its irrelevance. But negative feedback? The judgment of others? It must be addressed, it MUST be destroyed. Cue a silent golem that is stirred from slumber only by criticism as they are driven to mock, belittle, attack, or do whatever else is necessary to free their OWN veins from sludge. It's the only way they can know peace. We must look on and ponder the psychology of one who feels not compelled to say one word in response to heartfelt praise or gushing enthusiasm, yet at the slightest criticism leaps from the shadows to smirk and sneer. It is an interesting phenomenon to be sure. But is it the psychology I would want in my iron tyrant? No sirree!

So Lil withdrawal is a real thing so I started a replay with the transparency mod but seeing the choices without the box behind it is very disorienting and I don't think I will ever get used to it, it there a way to make it make only the text box transparent?
Click to expand...
I had the same problem. I received the transparency mod in the form of a file y_outline.rpy. If you also have that file, search it for a line ## choice button background. Comment out the two lines below (by prepending a hash symbol) like so:
Code: 
    # style choice_button:
        # background None
You can also delete these lines. Either way, delete the file y_outline.rpyc (this is a compilation artifact which will be regenerated) and start the program.

The mod loads after all other code, superseding previous settings in the original. By removing the choice_button entry there, we allow the original setting to prevail, and thus retain the classic pink smiley-face buttons.

If your transparency mod isn't the same file as mine, search the directory for the text style choice_button:. Wherever you find that line with background None beneath, just comment out or delete both lines, then delete the .rpyc version of the .rpy file you edited.

Further down the line you are given too much time with yourself and too little time with the person you love, you start having panic attacks imagining a future where it was all taken away and you start to blame them for letting you fall so badly for them. Yeah...
I guess it's just easy to forget that the obsessed delusional girl could either end up hurting herself badly or end up taking it out on others, turning yandere as to say. I dunno, rambling.

I thought it was a spoiled brat reaction but no, it was mother nostalgia. I guess I forgot that before the bubble wrap thing they probably didn't have much. So she grew up poor.

Ok, I take it back, redact those minus points from before... I'm not blind, I understand suddenly being rich doesn't solve all your problems. Internally, it probably causes a lot of other social problems. You probably realize that now that you can fix most of your problems with money but social problems can't really be fixed, you distance yourself from the real because the real is difficult. Might be how the dad is handling the situation and the mother ended up hurt too.

It's not just obsession for the sake of love... It's the lack of a father figure. Man, I'm talking too much about this but I suppose this is an important turning point. Also very fitting considering the title of the game.

Oof, that's... that's a very rough choice right there. I guess this is also the introduction to tough decisions. Stay with Ayane, risk hurting Sana, or go home and risk hurting Ayane. I mean, quantity wise, you would benefit more from staying behind but, I dunno... I will just play through it and see where it goes.

Well, it's a good thing Sana is a little oblivious and too trusting...
Also I kinda forgot just now that Ami is waiting for him to come home. I guess she was informed but still.

Going home is the cowards choice. Staying in risky but it is Sana. It would be a different story if Chika was the one feeling down and Yumi came home to see that... holy fuck I can only imagine.

The more I think about it, the more difficult it's starting to seem to just settle with Ayane's. Mikoto, Futaba, Ami and Ayane is all over him. You could easily separate from Miku, Rin, Maya and probably Sana. But something tells me Chika could be difficult and as much as she doesn't want to admit it, Yumi might be hurt about it too, probably feeling horrible knowing the whole job search wouldn't happen and she have her first kiss with him, even if the context was fucked up. Everyone else you he barely knows yet, but there is Sara... She's mature enough to accept the circumstances. I guess this is just the kinda dilemma you encounter when you get too close to too many people at the same time.

What kind of cursed option is that?

Oh, she's on her period, isn't she? Kirin's first event called "partners in crime", they get to the point of sitting at the couch in her home. She's done asking her question and he asks his, wondering why she acts like she wants sex but don't act like it. Then there was some acknowledgement and she went on about that's just how it is to be a woman and that she just can't right now. Like I'm 95% sure she's implying she can't because she's on her period and it's messing with what she wants and does not want to do.

Hmm, he either becomes the teacher of the second group of 10 girls, he stays the teacher of the current 10 girls, they somehow merge to form a group of 20, he gets fired, the game ends or something else. But that could be a long way from now.

His gone 3 months without knowing his the advisor of a manga club... How has no one including Ami not told him about this? Once again the plot fails me.

Ahh... So now we have two girls who hate calling you Daddy, only that selecting that for Ami apparently breaks the world.
Still not able to figure out what to have the characters call us. Having Sara call you daddy works just fine because she seems to be into it but I'm not sure about the others.
I... didn't expect that to work??? I select "brother" and that gave no reaction. Then I selected "big bro/brother" and that gave a reaction.
Seems she's not the only one who reacts to that one. You know, this is PRECISELY the reason why I wanted people to actually respond instead of saying "there are a few others". Yes, so WHAT ARE THEY? I am here for content, not trying to figure out everything. At least I'm making a separate save for the naming sequences so I can come back and check later...
Welp. The reactions to big bro are amusing.
Okay yeah, I am definitely lost. Ayane doesn't react to it but Sara and Futaba does.
Like is there a file I can check for a list of names with special interactions or something?

For some reason, this was the moment I decided to check the content on the computer and I gotta say, I'm mildly amused. Sana and Rin with Sana being the dominant one? That is indeed an unlikely situation. Also, I kinda expected the animations to be... worse. I guess I would have known there was animations in the game had I just checked the computer from the start of the game. Oh well.

Yeah ok. I'm gonna until much later to check the second bonus animation. I may have just accidentally confirmed the name of a "former teacher" to a student. I'm going to choose to hopefully forget this and pretend to have misinterpreted that. But I'm probably going to fail.

The room with clocks scene apparently used to have references to pokemon. Wonder what happened there... copyright or something. Game got too popular, dunno.

And Ayane walking in on him in the bathroom used to be A LOT longer and she was a lot more brave. And more stuff happened and... yeah. I wonder what the exact reasons were to cut out this entire thing. I can think of two primary reasons: This doesn't actually happen irl. And, it's not suppose to happen this fast and makes it seem more like a porn game rather than a game with porn. As it was described. Oh I guess another reason could also be that the dev wants it to be harder for Ayane to win him over and it pretty much happened at this moment. Maybe the scene can or does play again in the future instead.

Huh, and I guess the scene the scene where he walks in on Ami in the bath was cut because their relationship is actually closer from the start... actually I don't really know why it was cut out.
So the characters used to be standing a bit further away from the camera back then. Also that dialogue about him telling her she can "walk around the house naked for all I care" was reused later on".
Will continue checking these out later on. Wanna get on with the main story.

...Why the fuck did I just realized what the towns name stands for? Kumon-mi = cum on me... dude, it never crossed my mind to actually try to understand the name. Maybe my mind brushed across it once and then didn't commit...

Ah... I was about to say. I got so confused there. Why did the game decide to go back to normal mode when I'm playing autovn? Well apparently that's because this is a happy event. That's right, the happy event that's been suspiciously sitting in my hints section for 4 days now have finally triggered. Question is, does "rewrite" have anything to do with starting "everything is connected"?

Okay, I see. So this is the first reset event and this is also how you get the happy event. I was gonna ask about the shrine affection thing but it seems the txt I opened up at the start is now becoming relevant.

Oh... great. So now we are exploring THAT kind of fetish. I guess that part about many different fetishes appearing once or twice in the game wasn't false. It's rather suspicious that the length of the necks reach that height, don't you think?
That's not even a real word. Necroanthophilia.

Bro, I didn't expect to laugh during this, wtf!? Something about seeing Maya's expression got me laughing.

Huh. So I guess this nothing is beautiful game was actually made by Selebus before this game and it too is an existential horror?

Somehow seeing HOPE pop out of nowhere felt really weird. But I mean it makes sense. This thing is supposedly God... or was it god? I can't remember.

Ahhh, this feels nostalgic in a way. Hmm, Last Epoch? The end of time? You know... a very unusual place you end up several times throughout your journey. If this will follow the same pattern of several resets, several interactions with this Maya, asking different questions every time, then it feels familiar to things I've already seen. This concept is not new to me, but I can only remember Last Epoch and even that doesn't do this specific thing, only a very similar version. It could also be that it won't happen the way I think and this is just speculation.
The whole idea behind having experienced something an indeterminate amount of times and time looping is of course a common topic.

I hope I'm not gonna have to read the intro EVERY time.

I kind of expected the meeting with Maya to cause the memories to come back. I was so right.

Well I guess I sorta got the answer to the question of what will happen when the school year ends. It resets... for now.

Now how does that work? Time seems to twist and bend in all sorts of ways here. If time really did reset, she wouldn't have been taught those things by Makoto. But that means they are still that much closer to the end of the school year, but I'm assuming they aren't and they started out from day 1, which means... the previous owner of the body which is actually him were there when they were taught those things and he actually remembers being there... I really don't feel any wiser. This is a time anomaly that shouldn't be possible.

Half a year left, 3 months have past. I didn't really keep track but that seems like what this game originally started at. Hmmm. Yeah this is weird.
Not much changed today

Karin: Absolutely adorable how bad she is with boys.
Ayane: Her lack of a father figure hurts her more than I realized...


Tierlist and character notes and rules.

Being in the "not my type" tier is not necessarily fair but it's less work. Below that tier just means I haven't built a mental profile on the character yet. Children are measured by how fun they are to be around and how adorable they are, overlooking any other factor.

I don't hate any of the characters, I may just find them unremarkable and boring or can't see myself physically attracted to them.

The further top left the character is, the more I like them. Heavily affected by momentary bias.

If I didn't mention someone here, I probably don't have anything noteworthy to say yet.

Tierlists are hard, so the rankings may not be quite accurate to my true emotions and changes over time.

Sex scenes may affect where they are positioned based on momentary bias.

Okay, I see. So this is the first reset event and this is also how you get the happy event. I was gonna ask about the shrine affection thing but it seems the txt I opened up at the start is now becoming relevant.

Oh... great. So now we are exploring THAT kind of fetish. I guess that part about many different fetishes appearing once or twice in the game wasn't false. It's rather suspicious that the length of the necks reach that height, don't you think?
That's not even a real word. Necroanthophilia.

Bro, I didn't expect to laugh during this, wtf!? Something about seeing Maya's expression got me laughing.

Huh. So I guess this nothing is beautiful game was actually made by Selebus before this game and it too is an existential horror?

Somehow seeing HOPE pop out of nowhere felt really weird. But I mean it makes sense. This thing is supposedly God... or was it god? I can't remember.

Ahhh, this feels nostalgic in a way. Hmm, Last Epoch? The end of time? You know... a very unusual place you end up several times throughout your journey. If this will follow the same pattern of several resets, several interactions with this Maya, asking different questions every time, then it feels familiar to things I've already seen. This concept is not new to me, but I can only remember Last Epoch and even that doesn't do this specific thing, only a very similar version. It could also be that it won't happen the way I think and this is just speculation.
The whole idea behind having experienced something an indeterminate amount of times and time looping is of course a common topic.

I hope I'm not gonna have to read the intro EVERY time.

I kind of expected the meeting with Maya to cause the memories to come back. I was so right.

Well I guess I sorta got the answer to the question of what will happen when the school year ends. It resets... for now.

Now how does that work? Time seems to twist and bend in all sorts of ways here. If time really did reset, she wouldn't have been taught those things by Makoto. But that means they are still that much closer to the end of the school year, but I'm assuming they aren't and they started out from day 1, which means... the previous owner of the body which is actually him were there when they were taught those things and he actually remembers being there... I really don't feel any wiser. This is a time anomaly that shouldn't be possible.

Half a year left, 3 months have past. I didn't really keep track but that seems like what this game originally started at. Hmmm. Yeah this is weird.

Wow, that's kinda weird isn't it? Kirin is part of the main girls but Karin is not. Also that's the first new main girl added to the list.
Mc giving Karin a panic attack.
What could possibly make Ayane that sad? The only thing I could imagine is her catching the mc with someone else in a compromising position.
Oh that's not funny dude! Joking about being pregnant like that. Minus points for that one.
The pain of falling in love, huh? I guess this is the first taste of seeing how badly you could hurt the girls if they fall too heavily for you and they end up seeing you with someone else, only that you haven't seen that yet.

Further down the line you are given too much time with yourself and too little time with the person you love, you start having panic attacks imagining a future where it was all taken away and you start to blame them for letting you fall so badly for them. Yeah...
I guess it's just easy to forget that the obsessed delusional girl could either end up hurting herself badly or end up taking it out on others, turning yandere as to say. I dunno, rambling.
I thought it was a spoiled brat reaction but no, it was mother nostalgia. I guess I forgot that before the bubble wrap thing they probably didn't have much. So she grew up poor.
Ok, I take it back, redact those minus points from before... I'm not blind, I understand suddenly being rich doesn't solve all your problems. Tierlist and character notes and rules.

Being in the "not my type" tier is not necessarily fair but it's less work. Below that tier just means I haven't built a mental profile on the character yet. Children are measured by how fun they are to be around and how adorable they are, overlooking any other factor.

I don't hate any of the characters, I may just find them unremarkable and boring or can't see myself physically attracted to them.

The further top left the character is, the more I like them. Heavily affected by momentary bias.

If I didn't mention someone here, I probably don't have anything noteworthy to say yet.

Tierlists are hard, so the rankings may not be quite accurate to my true emotions and changes over time.

Sex scenes may affect where they are positioned based on momentary bias.

If the color of the tiles are the same, it means they are equally important.

What are some characters that surprised you with how much you ended up enjoying or liking them, for whatever reason?

I have a few examples. One is Rin. I didn't really know what to expect from her at first, but she absolutely won me over. She's a fun girl who deserves nothing but happiness. Her boobs are also no joke.

Kirin's development in later chapters is interesting, to say the least.

Ayane needs no introduction. She's way stronger than I thought possible and I'm kinda rooting for her.

Imani is hilarious and fun, and her and Sensei's relationship is endearing to me.

IDK, just curious to hear what you guys think. And did any girl who you didn't notice much at first become your best girl or waifu?
