Unfortunately all of this could be pointless since Selebus could just go "22 is my old game, 23 is LiL, and 24 is the next one".
Anyway, just food for thought. Maybe some of it makes sense.

Tierlist and character notes and rules.

Being in the "not my type" tier is not necessarily fair but it's less work. Below that tier just means I haven't built a mental profile on the character yet. Children are measured by how fun they are to be around and how adorable they are, overlooking any other factor.

I don't hate any of the characters, I may just find them unremarkable and boring or can't see myself physically attracted to them.

The further top left the character is, the more I like them. Heavily affected by momentary bias.

If I didn't mention someone here, I probably don't have anything noteworthy to say yet.

Tierlists are hard, so the rankings may not be quite accurate to my true emotions and changes over time.

Sex scenes may affect where they are positioned based on momentary bias.

DeSkel15 said:
I knew like 5 girls that'd flirt with Teachers, Drug Dealers, and Police, to get what they wanted, growing up. They'd also typically have boyfriends on top of that.

I know for sure, one was pregnant (I mean, the belly was an obvious give away). Can't tell you if the Teacher was the daddy, though.

I'm also not the social type even if people tended to group up around me. That's just from casual observation. (Albeit, I did tend to be around the "bad kids" and boy would the girls in LiL be different if Men and Drugs weren't so suspiciously absent in this game for the most part.)

Anyway, I definitely don't see Kirin as anything special in any way, shape, or form.

I'd think most girls in her position would do similar. She really just wants attention, and it's not like Sensei was a random person. She already had a good idea that he was a pervert (and one at an all girls school), and Ayane was someone she's had a petty grudge, and a crush on, for likely years, then the opportunity presented itself. If that opportunity never did, then they're still friends.

Hence why optionally, Kirin and Ayane are still friends. At least, until next update, lmao.
Click to expand...
That doesn't really equate imo. Obviously this discussion is lighthearted as we're just debating made up characters, so I'm not taking this seriously as it all just boils down to Selebus. However, I think the issue is not that girls wouldn't do this, but that she goes from 0 to 100 out of nowhere. This makes sense inside the resets, but not really in real life. While certainly possible to hit on a teacher for personal gain, to straight up flash him while having no experience whatsoever in sexual matters is uncanny. To go from that to sexual assault and blackmail is even more so.

Aside from that, and giving my two cents: I agree that Futaba is one of the most realistic ones, but rather than Kirin, I'd add Otoha to the mix.

In fact, for all my distaste of her, she behaves exactly like a common teenager. In what world wouldn't she develop a crush on Niki and "shoot her shot", as the youngsters say, given the chance? Rin, for all I love her, puts herself time and time again in a position to be taken advantage of, and that's what Otoha does. As, sadly, a lot would in her situation. "A girl is throwing herself at me, while the one I want doesn't even see me, and I can use this person to get some experience to maybe have a better shot at Niki? Count me in". I wasn't always a mature old goth chick, and I don't know if in Otoha's position (and mainly age) I'd have acted differently. At this point, he’s completely paralyzed, because the consequences in this world can be so horrific—and seemingly random.

Sana and Rin: Their fathers were never in their lives, so they wouldn't have had any connection to Akira.
Nodoka: I'm convinced that Nozomu can't be her father, but even if he was he probably wasn't part of her life. If Yuu is her father, she was born years after he left his family with Saki, so I don't know why she would know Akira.
Also, if it's any daughter of Nozomu, why would a play date with Ami be at Akira's house rather than Nozomu's? Akira and Nozomu don't get along and it's not like he could be trying to hide it from Sekai when Akira sucks at keeping secrets from her.
Yeah, she had very good reason to be worried about Sensei's reaction. This is from shortly after the first reset:

That's why she chickened out on the roof.

It's especially understandable when you take into account her abandonment issues and how she feels that the Arakawas are the only family she has now. She's absolutely terrified that Sensei is so opposed to being a father that he'll leave her (also taking Ami) when she tells him.
Click to expand...
Maya started showing up to tutoring lessons way after Noriko. If she was with Akira before Sekai's death it would make no sense for her to show up later. In fact, given that she meets Akira after running away from home, it would mean she'd be living in the Arakawa family home, which wouldn't make sense either with her later moving to the tutoring place.
Edit: Your older post makes sense, but I'm not convinced by it. I mean, I'm not convinced by it
without
a supernatural interference that puts a Maya there. If that's the case then I'm onboard.
Basically I don't think having Maya in his life fits the Akira that was in a relationship with both Sekai and Niki. If that wasn't an 8 year old though, and instead was a conjured up narrator Maya, then I'm cool with it.

This is just sad now. She's actually fucking traumatized. I can't believe Kirin would do something like that. Did that beach event with Chika Yumi and Chinami with the mc happen before the reset and that's why Chika is confused about it?

...you serious? THAT'S how she's gonna say it? uhhhhhhh...

Welp... That confession left me speechless... but that wasn't a right out rejection. Maybe there is a chance after all...? But I guess being reminded by the one you just confessed to that they are interested in someone else may contradict that wishful thinking...

Name of the game mentioned, but did it feel real? Not even a little bit. Maybe I was just too distracted.

What the fuck? I guess Futaba really DID get sick after all.

Well, I can't imagine staying up all night praying and only sleeping a couple hours did Maya any good.

Well he has only kissed 2 people in the second part of town and I'm not sure how Chika would react if she found out it was Yumi... and non consensual at that. It would be bad, like really bad.

This feels so incredibly and morally wrong! The moment you get home from the vacation after Rin confessed to Chika and getting indirectly rejected, the mc goes to finger and kiss Chika. Like what?

"G-good penis! I mean, good morning!" hmm, yep.

Maya find this failure of ours "interesting".

So anyway...

He doesn't want to go home. Don't make him go him, it's not a good idea.

That's a weird looking cat.

Same eye color, same bangs, maybe even a good portion of their hair is similar. Similar interests too. If I didn't know any better, I would say they are related, this Nodoka and Futaba.

Uhh, that could possibly be so bad that Futaba would rather jerk you off under the table in the library?

Ahh, Kirin is the manipulative kind. Secretly evil? There's gotta be a specific type she belongs to but I don't have the name.

Anyone else wished Chika would suggest visiting sick Yumi instead of watching over Chinami, or at the very least the mc would suggest it and be told to watch Chinami instead?

Hanging out with Chinami at her home.
Chinami is a weird child. Or maybe all children are like that.

Fucking bronies...
Bro, what are these options? Wtf, it worked, he actually got kicked out of the house for saying his a brony!

Think I accidentally enabled Spanish.
Wires and wires and wires and wires and wires.

Imagine how funny this game would be if there were no startles and spooky images and it was all just weird stuff like this.

Kirin: Perhaps a bit manipulative and evil.


Tierlist and character notes and rules.

Being in the "not my type" tier is not necessarily fair but it's less work. Below that tier just means I haven't built a mental profile on the character yet. Children are measured by how fun they are to be around and how adorable they are, overlooking any other factor.

I don't hate any of the characters, I may just find them unremarkable and boring or can't see myself physically attracted to them.

The further top left the character is, the more I like them. Heavily affected by momentary bias.

Sex scenes may affect where they are positioned based on momentary bias.

spoilers.title: Tierlist
spoilers.html:
Kirin: Perhaps a bit manipulative and evil.


Tierlist and character notes and rules.

Being in the "not my type" tier is not necessarily fair but it's less work. Below that tier just means I haven't built a mental profile on the character yet. Children are measured by how fun they are to be around and how adorable they are, overlooking any other factor.

I don't hate any of the characters, I may just find them unremarkable and boring or can't see myself physically attracted to them.

The further top left the character is, the more I like them. Heavily affected by momentary bias.

If I didn't mention someone here, I probably don't have anything noteworthy to say yet.

Tierlists are hard, so the rankings may not be quite accurate to my true emotions and changes over time.

Sex scenes may affect where they are positioned based on momentary bias.

If the color of the tiles are the same, it means they are equally important.


Some edited since yesterday.
Yumi: I can't WAIT to see how the story with her escalates. Every time he messes with her, it's so fun and I like her appearance too.
Ayane: She's obsessed with you. Her lack of a father figure hurts her more than I realized...
Ami: Red hair, she loves you.
Chika: I expected an annoying gyaru girl who acts way too popular but I got someone chill and down to earth, fun to be around.
Makoto: I love it when he messes with her. I slightly dislike her hair and how studious she is.
Sana: Very precious.
Sara: Hot mom, I repeat, hot mom!
Maya: The mystery behind her is intriguing.
Miku: Not into tomboys.
Futaba: Not into big girls or big tits.
Rin: Nice hair. A bit bland unless Chika is around. Also seem to have a bit of a wingman personality.
Kirin: Surprisingly flirtatious... and intimidatingly so.
Karin: Absolutely adorable how bad she is with boys.
Chinami: So adorable! Must protecc!
Molly: She can be anywhere.
Haruka: Breasts are way too large for my liking but otherwise she's ok.
Kaori: Her eccentric personality is growing on me. Not a fan of the spider tattoo.
Tsuneyo: This one is rough... extremely sheltered type.

I personally don't think the game is really in danger of being cancelled by a mob from X, of all places.
  1. The only people really shocked by the content, at least so far, would probably be normies anyway, and I don't see normies finding their way to an adult visual novel. Besides, X is a cesspool of weirdos and people very far away from being normal - and I'm typing this on a porn game message board.
  2. The stuff isn't really all that bad so far anyway. In a world where loli hentai is mainstream in at least Japan, I don't see nieche stuff like this raising too many eyebrows.
  3. The platform (subscribestar) probably wouldn't care much. If anything, they probably already received some pushback on other projects I imagine, given the kind of other stuff they feature on there.
At the end of the day, anyone interested enough to look into the game deep enough to notice the problematic stuff would probably already have to be a gooner. And gooners typically don't want to raise attention to them gooning and would not care anyway.

The only thing that could realistically cause a problem to the development, in my opinion, is if somehow Selebus himself would receive some negative attention. There have been examples in the past where stuff like that can happen, so I'm keeping my fingers crossed that he is actually a decent enough guy to not do anything stupid irl.

This can be solved by hypothesizing a few scenarios without involving anything supernatural:

1. I can assume that the nature of Maya visiting pre-accident and the nature of Maya encountering post-accident being different. For example, the playdate took place due to a normal visit between the families, then Maya showed up to Akira's tutoring castle a few years later due to her running away from her family.

2. Or, the first playdate was also a result of a runaway attempt; Arakawa family found her, let Ami keep her company for a little while without telling Ami what happened, before locating the Makinami family and sending Maya back.

3. [Be creative here]

I will acknowledge that I have zero proof to support anything above and all of it is essentially creative writing. But, I will say that the mysterious playdate girl being Maya is, for the time being, the "least unlikely" option. This is because, compared to Maya, the past of other main cast girls are a lot clearer, leaving considerably smaller wiggle room to insert any hypothesized scenario that can make sense of this playdate without clashing into preestablished knowledge about the said girls (Simply put, in my eye Maya as a candidate will survive the most rounds of process of elimination).

Like the case of Rin and Sana you brought up; there would be so many "but if this is true, what about that?" type of follow up questions that will plummet their chances of being the playdate girl. Besides, I didn't think being a potential bastard of Nozomu was a required element that facilitated the said playdate (I understand that you're trying to find candidates with at least one additional layer of connection to the Arakawas). Thus, even if Nodoka's past is less clear and more suspicious than the aforementioned two, her chance is as big as the thread's favorite Otoha: low.

Maya on the other hand, her past history is highly connected to Akira, and is almost entirely unclear or well certified, and Maya herself has been shown to conceals information constantly even in the present days. Combining those with how other main cast girls (plus their moms if applicable) interact with Ami and Sensei in the current time, no other main cast girl has a suspicion level nearly as high as Maya.

You'd notice that I also assume that the playdate girl will exclusively turn out to be one of the main cast girls. Breaking this assumption is very easy and realistic, but narratively makes little sense. Because of that, this playdate girl's relevance to Sensei and Ami will also have to be high enough if such under the radar reunion is true. Noriko might fit here under this lens, but I simply find dyeing a less than 7 year old girl's hair bizarre ever since her pink hair was proven to be natural (unless this in fact is a culturally common thing and I am massively unaware of it, or unless there in fact exists a possibly good enough reason for a preschool Noriko to dye her hair).

PS. I am not sure how valid the following can be, but I also assume that Sekai would know who this playdate girl is, and ghost Sekai has made comments on two prime candidates: Noriko and Nodoka. She doesn't seem to recognize neither (but yea asking a ghost mom to remember a girl from a playdate with your daughter well before she bit the dust might just be too much to ask)

In 35.0, best known as the "Death of Maya Prime" and "that fucking puzzle sucked" chapter, the opening event is Eggside Octopus. After the first black screen, with a patented pause starting it out, the dialog starts.

None of this makes logical sense just reading it as is, so there must be more to it, I thought.

Figured someone would've mentioned it at some point - and apologies if someone already did - but nothing of value related to it appeared when searching the event name.

Have at it, code-breakers/lore lovers.

Day 12 character count 2039. This one is exceptionally short. I got partially distracted by another game so there's not much to read but progress nonetheless.
First time he acknowledges the smilies. He doesn't like them, I agree they are disturbing, but that is most likely the point.

Have Tsuneyo been talking to Maya recently...?

That might have been one if not the first time the game decided to ruin a laugh moment by halting the music and giving a static right after. That strange white haired girl appeared again, but this time in person...

Oh don't tell me... She's that cryptic kind that shows up when you least expect it to spell doom, never telling you her name, messing with your head while creepy music plays in the background only to disappear as soon as she appeared... or something similar.
Quite accurate. Bet we will eventually know her name tho... probably.

Kinda weird for him to choose to interact with Futaba of all people when she's clearly sick and sleeping.

It wouldn't be fever if she's keeping it a secret. You wouldn't be the cause of her illness if she doesn't assert herself to push you out and inform you that you being around makes it worse. It's something else and sooner or later she will say it.

Rin is in THAT mood again. Welp.

I would be very concerned if Chika's genes was passed down to Chinami. That would be their mother's doing.

Chinami is a menace to pig society.

Being blackmailed by a kid... Chinami is a menace to sensei society too.

How dare this tiny human insult hes reading talent!

What's in the box, Maya? WHAT'S IN THE FUCKING BOX?

That static got me again...

AAAND again. Another static from one of Maya's events. Am I training myself to not get angry at startles? Perhaps. Do I like it? Nope.

Mc saw the chance and took it, calling Maya a princess.
(this day have been filled with lots of Maya events for some reason)

How much you wanna bet Maya brought us to this maid cafe because we are meant to meet Uta?

Are maids the mc's weakness? Is it the roleplay cosplay fantasy he likes?

I had no idea what to expect from an event titled "FLAVOR BEAM!"

Turns out I didn't make a single manual save today. No idea how that happened.

Uta: Absolutely adorable maid.


Tierlist and character notes and rules.

Being in the "not my type" tier is not necessarily fair but it's less work. Below that tier just means I haven't built a mental profile on the character yet. Children are measured by how fun they are to be around and how adorable they are, overlooking any other factor.

I don't hate any of the characters, I may just find them unremarkable and boring or can't see myself physically attracted to them.

The further top left the character is, the more I like them. Heavily affected by momentary bias.

If I didn't mention someone here, I probably don't have anything noteworthy to say yet.

Tierlists are hard, so the rankings may not be quite accurate to my true emotions and changes over time.

Sex scenes may affect where they are positioned based on momentary bias.

If the color of the tiles are the same, it means they are equally important.


Some edited since yesterday.

Ayane: She's obsessed with you. Her lack of a father figure hurts her more than I realized...
Ami: Red hair, she loves you.
Chika: I expected an annoying gyaru girl who acts way too popular but I got someone chill and down to earth, fun to be around.
Makoto: I love it when he messes with her. I slightly dislike her hair and how studious she is.
Sana: Very precious.
Sara: Hot mom, I repeat, hot mom!
Maya: The mystery behind her is intriguing.
Miku: Not into tomboys.
Futaba: Not into big girls or big tits.
Rin: Nice hair. A bit bland unless Chika is around. Also seem to have a bit of a wingman personality.
Kirin: Surprisingly flirtatious... and intimidatingly so. Perhaps a bit manipulative and evil.
Karin: Absolutely adorable how bad she is with boys.
Chinami: So adorable! Must protecc!
Molly: She can be anywhere.
Haruka: Breasts are way too large for my liking but otherwise she's ok.
Kaori: Her eccentric personality is growing on me. Not a fan of the spider tattoo.
Tsuneyo: This one is rough... extremely sheltered type.

spoilers.html:
First time he acknowledges the smilies. He doesn't like them, I agree they are disturbing, but that is most likely the point.

Have Tsuneyo been talking to Maya recently...?

That might have been one if not the first time the game decided to ruin a laugh moment by halting the music and giving a static right after. That strange white haired girl appeared again, but this time in person...

Oh don't tell me... She's that cryptic kind that shows up when you least expect it to spell doom, never telling you her name, messing with your head while creepy music plays in the background only to disappear as soon as she appeared... or something similar.
Quite accurate. Bet we will eventually know her name tho... probably.

Kinda weird for him to choose to interact with Futaba of all people when she's clearly sick and sleeping.

It wouldn't be fever if she's keeping it a secret. You wouldn't be the cause of her illness if she doesn't assert herself to push you out and inform you that you being around makes it worse. It's something else and sooner or later she will say it.

Rin is in THAT mood again. Welp.

I would be very concerned if Chika's genes was passed down to Chinami. That would be their mother's doing.

Chinami is a menace to pig society.

Being blackmailed by a kid... Chinami is a menace to sensei society too.

How dare this tiny human insult hes reading talent!

What's in the box, Maya? WHAT'S IN THE FUCKING BOX?

That static got me again...

AAAND again. Another static from one of Maya's events. Am I training myself to not get angry at startles? Perhaps. Do I like it? Nope.

Mc saw the chance and took it, calling Maya a princess.
(this day have been filled with lots of Maya events for some reason)

How much you wanna bet Maya brought us to this maid cafe because we are meant to meet Uta?

Are maids the mc's weakness? Is it the roleplay cosplay fantasy he likes?

I had no idea what to expect from an event titled "FLAVOR BEAM!"

Turns out I didn't make a single manual save today. No idea how that happened.

It's still up in the air.
Current evidence suggests that Noriko saw Maya and Akira. Especially from replaying, Noriko makes mention of "doing things in public with him" might be a problem, referencing a possible first time that it had already happened (and she failed to notice it being a problem then). Maya talks about Noriko being unable to keep a secret, and her being somewhat involved in why they had to leave the old district, and how Maya had to deal with this situation rather than him. Then there's the "promise" of her keeping to the old district and Maya not going there (something that Noriko seems to have forgotten at least part of, or is just lying about - in the sense that Maya takes this way more seriously than her, and she says that she can't recall doing anything to piss Maya off).

What exactly Noriko saw then we don't know. It's possible that Maya kissed Akira in public or something in order to get him to move away from the old district, and that she made that decision because Noriko was about to inform her family that they were in a relationship, or that Noriko was about to try to form a relationship with him as well, idk.

Other possibilities, raised by other regulars, talk about not being Maya at all. But rather either Ami or Sekai. I don't remember the full scope of these possibilities, I'm inclined to believe that it had something to do with Maya.

Mind you, this time that Noriko sees him is likely to be in a point in the timeline where Sekai was already dead, and their tutoring had already stopped - because she mentions that he disappeared, then there was this incident, and then their next meeting was at school.

spoilers.title: Possibilities
spoilers.html:
Current evidence suggests that Noriko saw Maya and Akira. Especially from replaying, Noriko makes mention of "doing things in public with him" might be a problem, referencing a possible first time that it had already happened (and she failed to notice it being a problem then). Maya talks about Noriko being unable to keep a secret, and her being somewhat involved in why they had to leave the old district, and how Maya had to deal with this situation rather than him. Then there's the "promise" of her keeping to the old district and Maya not going there (something that Noriko seems to have forgotten at least part of, or is just lying about - in the sense that Maya takes this way more seriously than her, and she says that she can't recall doing anything to piss Maya off).

What exactly Noriko saw then we don't know. It's possible that Maya kissed Akira in public or something in order to get him to move away from the old district, and that she made that decision because Noriko was about to inform her family that they were in a relationship, or that Noriko was about to try to form a relationship with him as well, idk.

Other possibilities, raised by other regulars, talk about not being Maya at all. But rather either Ami or Sekai. I don't remember the full scope of these possibilities, I'm inclined to believe that it had something to do with Maya.

Mind you, this time that Noriko sees him is likely to be in a point in the timeline where Sekai was already dead, and their tutoring had already stopped - because she mentions that he disappeared, then there was this incident, and then their next meeting was at school.

(My thoughts upon reading both DeSkel's and aramaug's points on the upside down house - please correct me, as I find this topic hard to parse).

Okay so, we know that there are five girls in the upside down house.
It would be simple if they were Saki Sakurazaka, Miu Miyahara, Reina Ritsushima, Kyoko Nagasawa and Ai Ariyoshi. Three of these are mothers to our current characters, Saki is mother to Akira and Nozomu. Miu is mother to Sekai. Kyoko is mother to Nodoka. Ai being mother to Niki and Noriko would be a stretch at this point because we only have her hair color. No idea about Reina, is she the one with lavender hair (thus potentially Futaba's mother)? Or is that Yuko? (more on that later)

However, unfortunately, it seems that that theory doesn't really hold because as it has been pointed out, we should also deal with Shiori, Setsuna and Himawari. I think it's interesting if the people from the upside down house were Akira's children but isn't the upside down house Terminal 22? I would have assumed that it was the house near a lake, and if it is, then it would also be where it all began way before Akira was born (and where we meet Miu and Yuu).

I think it's also fair to assume that the events from the upside down house reset, just as the events from 23. Thus being dead for some time is just a temporary condition. There's also another figure in the upside down house other than the girls, which is "the father that sets the rules".

Finally, we might need to examine the possibility that these girls could have multiple names. We do see DOUBT at one point right? So maybe Reina and Yuko are the same person, or even Kyoko and Shiori - or maybe, they're not the same person, but the cast of the upside down house changes.

Regardless, it seems that people have escaped 22. I mean, their children are born, right? They left the upside down house. Other than Kyoko, which left her mind behind. Yet the Miu that we meet does not seem to have experienced real issues (she says only Yuu is the weird one), and she's already pregnant with Sekai by that point. So if she was to be prisoner to some house, surely that would have happened before, no?
Again, I still find this topic confusing.

What is OOT
Click to expand...
Out of Touch.

Like this game, an ambitious adult cosmic/existential horror harem game* with deep lore, a sexy, diverse cast of compelling characters and a sprawling plot.Both are plotty stories with sex, rather than porn stories withh some plot. Both games are well written by native English speakers, are set in Japan, and have a multi-year history of steady development.

OoT’s main differences from LiL:
  1. No loli (except in one flashback); there’s only one character who’s portrayed as less than 18
  2. No backstory of sexual abuse and incest
  3. Both are funny, but OoT is less snarky/sardonic
  4. It takes a while to start getting sex scenes (but once they come…. Whew!)
  5. The MC is a goof, but he’s not a horrible human being
  6. The creators don’t seem to be assholes
* Though there are some combat and sandbox sequences, it’s really a kinetic novel—there aren’t any substantive choices. Mind, I don’t think LiL has many, and I don’t think Sel has done much with them to this point.

Reina might be the mother of Sara and Ai the mother of Haruka (Or Niki and Noriko), but that's just based off them having similar looks, presumably.

Yuu Narrator - "This is Reina. She's probably the most ordinary person I know."

Yuu Narrator - "In fact, she's absolutely terrified of everything."
Miu - "Why didn't you answer the door? I thought you were dead in here."
(Chapter 3 'Rain King' Happy Event)
At times. They may have several names due to this.

There seems to be certain rules they also have to follow. Perhaps these Rules were made by Balaam the prophet/papa?

Amy - "Rumor has it that a long time ago, when the mall was first coming into existence, a small group of some...weird kind of entity or something snuck in and started nesting around here."
- "I also heard that if they suck up enough, they can manipulate their bodies into appearing human! Meaning some of them could be here right now and we'd have no idea!"

Overall: The UDH (and whatever is going on with The Mall) is still a mystery.

I also have to wonder if we're actually playing as a "Shapeshifter" that got lost in their role as Sensei/Akira, or something.

Edit: I kind of like my Christmas hat, tbh.

Surely the mc isn't so cruel as to make Ami do all the work and not even give her the money to get something new to wear partially for him, right?

Ami is preparing her yandere arch.

Chika cock-shock, love it.
"It's bigger than my little sister" She says while referring to his dick.

And now, for something completely different.
Cases of the mc being a good guy so far.
Lets the students do whatever they want making the studying the students responsibility. Yeah, it sounds bad, but Makoto wants to be a teacher so this is her opportunity to be that.
He ummm, let the students organize a vacation, which they could have technically done by themselves but whatever.
He pays Chika's and Chinami's phone bill, technically Yumi's too but she doesn't know that and for her it probably doesn't matter... unless he pays 100% instead of her original 50%? That was never mentioned I think.
He tried to help Yumi look for a job... tried being the keyword. Also paid for some of her meals.
Supporting local business, Sara's bar, Haruka's cafe, Tsuneyo's noodle restaurant, Uta at the maid cafe and Maki's porn shop (technically thanks to Makoto even tho she refuses to sell him anything).
The soccer team can keep practicing thanks to the mc's coach role.
He finally acknowledged Ayane which the previous him didn't. It may not seem like a good thing but given how obsessed she is with him, it might as well be.
Takes care of Chinami every now and then.
Helps Sana become better at speaking and opening up, also helped her befriend Rin so she's less lonely.
Carried Maya's boxes and paid for her food I guess? Although hes probably done more harm for her than good if you asked her.
Made Futaba feel desired and confident in herself.
Supported Rin when she's at her worst.
There's probably some other actions he's done that can be seen as good but this is still a noticeable list of things that while there are ulterior motives are still good action.
Anyway... back to game.

Batard-uncle, why is that so funny to me?

Chika's bracelet appears to be jiggling during the handjob animation.

I wonder what it's actually like for the girls to be head patted for that long.
Chika is clearly getting angrier and angrier by this so it must be some kind of torture.
Poor Chika... Being brought to orgasm via head patting.

I just now discover Haruka's morning animated doggystyle at the cafe? I wonder how many more scenes I've unlocked that I haven't seen yet... probably not many.

Hmm, I wonder if Rin is gonna change her hair style. Just a random though.

I guess he should have also told Uta to pretend he had been here many times before...

Oh god, wtf? Hearing Uta (the maid) talk about how her brother shot the deer in the backyard and then they ate them makes it seem like this maid is not quite so pure.

Attack-hug? You mean surprise-hug?

I was like "Yeah, why is it called last ditch effort and not last stitch effort?" then proceeded to say that somewhere. One person said something about trench warfare. Fast forward in the game just a bit and there it is, it's a war reference. It makes sense but only when referring to ditches I guess.

So there is a chance... If being caring and affectionate then that makes you cool, huh?

"hydrothermopoly" the "holy heck, I'm so cold" disease.

That last face Ami was making... fuck that.

spoilers.title: Tierlist
spoilers.html:
I may forgive characters over time for a past mistake, bumping them back up.

A character most likely won't lose their position just because I haven't seen them enough in a while.



Tierlist and character notes and rules.

Being in the "not my type" tier is not necessarily fair but it's less work. Below that tier just means I haven't built a mental profile on the character yet. Children are measured by how fun they are to be around and how adorable they are, overlooking any other factor.

I don't hate any of the characters, I may just find them unremarkable and boring or can't see myself physically attracted to them.

The further top left the character is, the more I like them. Heavily affected by momentary bias.

If I didn't mention someone here, I probably don't have anything noteworthy to say yet.

Tierlists are hard, so the rankings may not be quite accurate to my true emotions and changes over time.

Sex scenes may affect where they are positioned based on momentary bias.

If the color of the tiles are the same, it means they are equally important.

In the upside down house discussion, we brought up the list of people that Pareidolia gave "special thanks" to:
The first three girls are from Nothing is Beautiful, and Kyoko and Ai are referenced as residents of the upside down house both in game and on the twitter. Balaam the prophet is a mystery, however.

I think there's one other time that Balaam has been indirectly referenced, and maybe it will give a clue to his (or her?) identity. When a panicking Ami calls Sensei from the old district, there's a flashback to the bus ride backwards and a narrator says they're giving us a "password".

The 23:19 on the negative image could be a bible verse, especially given the following discussion of God. As it happens, there are actually two verses of that number with connections to LiL, and I'm guessing Sel intended to refer to both of them.
  • Numbers 23:19 is by far the top result if you search for "bible 23:19". It's a message from God that is spoken by the prophet Balaam and has similar themes to the bus ride discussion.
  • Exodus 23:19 gives an injunction forbidding cooking a kid (goat) in its mother's milk.
Here's the Exodus verse:

In the event where the 23:19 is shown, we're given hints that Ami's mind is being influenced by some version of Sekai, and of course Sekai is also largely the subject of "Mother's Milk". So in the context of LiL we could parse this as a metaphor warning against letting Ami be corrupted by Sekai.

Here's the Numbers verse with surrounding context:

Sensei also talks about how God is fundamentally different from humans. Ami asks what happens if you defy God (which Sensei pointedly doesn't answer), which fits with the idea of god fulfilling his promises - God has promised to erase Sensei if he doesn't take something that doesn't belong to him.

Based on this scene, I'm wondering about a couple of possibilities for Balaam's identity. The first is Sensei himself, with Sensei's message about God on the bus being a parallel to Balaam's message about God in Numbers. Furthermore, Sensei isn't speaking his own opinion, so maybe he's instead repeating the word of God, spoken through his prophet.

The second possibility is Sekai, who shows up right after the bus ride. She seems to have had a connection with Pareidolia dating back to when she was still alive, and Ghost Sekai often shows up to repeat things Pareidolia has said, i.e. spread the word of God as his prophet. In addition, Sensei talking about God ends with him stating that Sekai is "with God now" and he sees her with Pareidolia's red moon.

Of course, Balaam could still be Yuu given he hears God's voice in Nothing is Beautiful and Saki, Miu, and Reina are his love interests. But it's hard to see a connection to Yuu in this event.
I also have a question: do we have any idea what password the narrator is referring to? This happens before the reset with Ami's laptop password "mom", which I never figured out how we were supposed to know without guessing, so maybe it's that - but how are we supposed to get "mom" out of the image? "23:19 -> Exodus -> mother's milk -> mom" seems far too convoluted, but I can't think of anything else.

Most of us haven't played Nothing is Beautiful, it is unfinished. I mean, it certainly will add some info, but the essentials are that Yuu (Akira's/Sekai's father) is the player, and his love interests are Miu (Sekai's mother), Saki (Akira's mother) and Reina. All info is info I guess, but it isn't needed to understand LiL.

The upside down house is from LiL. It is a recurring tv show/movie, and sometimes a dream, about 5 girls in a boarded up house. What sets it apart from other LiL lore is that it seems disconnected from our characters/current events (TERMINAL 23). Recently we had confirmation that TERMINAL 22 is the world where Yuu was still young and Miu was pregnant with Sekai. Nao-chan also says that it's Akira's home (meaning that Akira himself is not from 23 originally, but from 22). What that means exactly isn't clear yet.

Aditionally, we don't know if the house by the lake is the upside down house. The house by the lake is relevant because it's referenced as where "everything began long before Akira was born". This would fit with the overall events known about the upside down house, and TERMINAL 22 is a house by the lake. But this still needs confirmation.

Edit: Also, it's weird because Nao-chan sends Akira to a place that shouldn't exist anymore:



when he's sent to 22





which by the way should be at least the second time he's been to 22

The upside down house is from LiL. It is a recurring tv show/movie, and sometimes a dream, about 5 girls in a boarded up house. What sets it apart from other LiL lore is that it seems disconnected from our characters/current events (TERMINAL 23). Recently we had confirmation that TERMINAL 22 is the world where Yuu was still young and Miu was pregnant with Sekai. Nao-chan also says that it's Akira's home (meaning that Akira himself is not from 23 originally, but from 22). What that means exactly isn't clear yet.
Aditionally, we don't know if the house by the lake is the upside down house. The house by the lake is relevant because it's referenced as where "everything began long before Akira was born". This would fit with the overall events known about the upside down house, and TERMINAL 22 is a house by the lake. But this still needs confirmation.

aramaug said:
In the upside down house discussion, we brought up the list of people that Pareidolia gave "special thanks" to:
View attachment 4369737
The first three girls are from Nothing is Beautiful, and Kyoko and Ai are referenced as residents of the upside down house both in game and on the twitter. Balaam the prophet is a mystery, however.

I think there's one other time that Balaam has been indirectly referenced, and maybe it will give a clue to his (or her?) identity. When a panicking Ami calls Sensei from the old district, there's a flashback to the bus ride backwards and a narrator says they're giving us a "password".
View attachment 4368787 View attachment 4368789 View attachment 4368791
View attachment 4369227 View attachment 4369230 View attachment 4369231
The 23:19 on the negative image could be a bible verse, especially given the following discussion of God. As it happens, there are actually two verses of that number with connections to LiL, and I'm guessing Sel intended to refer to both of them.
  • Numbers 23:19 is by far the top result if you search for "bible 23:19". It's a message from God that is spoken by the prophet Balaam and has similar themes to the bus ride discussion.
  • Exodus 23:19 gives an injunction forbidding cooking a kid (goat) in its mother's milk.
Here's the Exodus verse:
View attachment 4369234
In the event where the 23:19 is shown, we're given hints that Ami's mind is being influenced by some version of Sekai, and of course Sekai is also largely the subject of "Mother's Milk". So in the context of LiL we could parse this as a metaphor warning against letting Ami be corrupted by Sekai.

Here's the Numbers verse with surrounding context:
View attachment 4369247
Sensei also talks about how God is fundamentally different from humans. Ami asks what happens if you defy God (which Sensei pointedly doesn't answer), which fits with the idea of god fulfilling his promises - God has promised to erase Sensei if he doesn't take something that doesn't belong to him.

Based on this scene, I'm wondering about a couple of possibilities for Balaam's identity. The first is Sensei himself, with Sensei's message about God on the bus being a parallel to Balaam's message about God in Numbers. Furthermore, Sensei isn't speaking his own opinion, so maybe he's instead repeating the word of God, spoken through his prophet.

The second possibility is Sekai, who shows up right after the bus ride. She seems to have had a connection with Pareidolia dating back to when she was still alive, and Ghost Sekai often shows up to repeat things Pareidolia has said, i.e. spread the word of God as his prophet. In addition, Sensei talking about God ends with him stating that Sekai is "with God now" and he sees her with Pareidolia's red moon.

Of course, Balaam could still be Yuu given he hears God's voice in Nothing is Beautiful and Saki, Miu, and Reina are his love interests. But it's hard to see a connection to Yuu in this event.
I also have a question: do we have any idea what password the narrator is referring to? This happens before the reset with Ami's laptop password "mom", which I never figured out how we were supposed to know without guessing, so maybe it's that - but how are we supposed to get "mom" out of the image? "23:19 -> Exodus -> mother's milk -> mom" seems far too convoluted, but I can't think of anything else.
Click to expand...
Complete tangent: that verse from Exodus is the reason that kosher Jewish folks don’t eat fleischig (meat) with milschig (dairy).

So maybe Sel was tellling us no ham and cheese sandwiches?

posts.content_html_raw:
LoveRedHairedGirl said:
Well, let's discuss, I dunno, LiL at Eternum thread as well then. And we should keep discussing it for 10+ messages in a row! yeah! Sounds great.
Click to expand...
Of all the English Ren'py games I played after LiL in search of something which captured a modicum of its greatness, Eternum probably faired the best. By the point I reached it I was happy just to see something written in what felt like native English, and it has nice production values to boot. The problem for me was that (as is so often the case), the character psychology ended up just a bit too underbaked to be engaging for a long period of time. The protagonist himself being a nothingburger was a big negative, but the heroines getting blander over time (or perhaps - not introducing any freshness after their introduction) was of course the real killer. A cloud of grimness fell over me as I trudged further and further into the game realizing that, far from learning more about the characters, I was simply observing the author shift gears into romance and sex mode dot exe. The clearest demonstration of this shallow writing, though, is best observed in the side characters rather than the main characters; there we consistently see cruel, bully-ish depictions of cardboard cutouts meant to be nothing more than stepping stones for the protagonist to grind the heels of his feet into. You can tell a lot about an author by how they treat side characters: are they jokes or do they feel like believable parts of the world? (With some consideration given to parodies and one-offs and so on). It is only with a roll of my eyes I point to Sara in Lessons in Love here, although I really do not want to fellate Selebus on this matter in particular: imagine a world where Sara is like a comical milf stereotype and then over 3 million words she is basically only used for sexo if not immediately forgotten.

All of the above is merely a preface for what I find a fairly funny happenstance, though. As it happens I was detailing my English VN journey to my fellow Japanese VN fans as a sort of farcical, ahem, 'kino journey' as the lads may call it on Discord (though far be it from me to spam such an uncouth word). And remarkably, almost every Japanese chad was FAR MORE intrigued by Eternum than Lessons in love. In the end, by brokering points (a sort of trade system where you offer X amounts of points for completing a game, and then those points can be brokered to force you to play a game), I was successful in coercing three Japanese gamers to play Lessons in Love (thereby, I might add, securing Selebus a smooth $15 extra in revenue a month, though he would thank me for that with a swift banhammer if we ever met eye-to-eye as men), but that is another matter entirely.

For some extremely thought-provoking reason, almost every screenshot or clip of Lessons in Love I sent inspired ire and mockery. I am no amateur when it comes to live-blogging; I knew to pick the best angles and best lines to give a biased picture of the game. I even have 10 VNDB screenshots lined up which would be sure to triple the turnover rate from the VNDB page, but at the last moment I saw that Selebus had hand-selected the existing screenshots, and although I have implied this in the past I would like to re-emphasize that the selection is totally garbage in what I can only imagine to be an intentional effort to filter out potentially judgmental players, but I'm getting ahead of myself again. The point is, almost every positive aspect of Lessons in Love is something that seems to exist only in context; as a base example, to laugh at spaghetti jokes one has to go through Sana's events and spend like 50 hours in the ambient mind space of 'the spaghetti incident' to finally laugh when the food competition happens and she cries at spaghetti. You can't just link the spaghetti incident. Similarly, perhaps we can say that Maya events in Chapter 2 are "high cinema" that belong in a museum along other works of art, but they have of course NO IMPACT out side of context - without having played LiL for 70+ hours, it will really mean nothing when Maya tears up and says, 'Even though you're the most disgusting person in the world,' positioned in front of lights in a very meaningful location. This is to say that it is an EXCRUCIATING EFFORT to convey to Japanese chads the quality of Lessons in Love, especially with little aid from the big man himself. Everything comes off as "cringe" or "meme humor" (to say nothing of how they have 0 exposure to Koikatsu graphics used in this manner, although big leaps were made when the comic 愚かで勤勉な私たちは blew up in Japanese twitter). That's why I ended up brokering points; there's almost no other way to convince them but by physical force.

Eternum, on the other hand, caught on like fire. Everybody fucked loved it. I couldn't believe it. From my perspective I had just shot blood from every pore as I strained to hold up the world like Atlas, then in the next moment had a horde of duders offering to share the burden. Every single clip I posted engendered mass attention and laughs. Every single screenshot had at least one person asking 'source?'. Humiliatingly enough, some would even make comments like, 'Why did you have that whole Lessons in Love arc for a month if you could have been playing this.' I like to think that if Selebus were present to witness it he would have tightened his hand into a fist and trembled for at least three seconds. It was that distinct, and in fact one guy even came from the woodworks to say he was a long-term fan of Eternum, which was crazy since of course Lessons in Love had existed in beyond obscurity; some still doubt its existence.

This proved to be a matter of deep contemplation to me. What exactly was the difference here? I could remove myself as a variable since I came to this with the same expertise and methods to the same audience in the same climate. The difference had to be the games. So I thought and thought and... honestly, it's not that complicated. Eternum's own shallowness is what made it so much more universally appealing at a glance, and while that seems like a salty or backhanded insult, that is not my intention. Rather, there are basically no jokes like the spaghetti, and there are minimal long-running contextual sources of humor or pog that you have to be immersed in the game to understand. Everything is immediate, direct, in-your-face, and so on. Alas, I do not believe F95 handles clips well, but I will attempt to link 3 streamable examples.

https://streamable.com/6jr2jj
https://streamable.com/1s11d8
https://streamable.com/edxxar

What we see here are instances of what in the Japanese community we refer to as "high quality 演出," with 演出 being like a mix of 'scene direction' and 'production value.' Essentially a scene that looks high-effort and good will be said to have good 演出. Anyway, what Eternum lacks in deep or meaningful characterization it has in spades in 演出, and an outside observer will need little understanding of any lore or contextual humor to appreciate this. Link a picture of an artful discussion between Nodoka and Sensei, you run a fine line of people rolling their eyes. Link a clip of the camera spinning like crazy as dark souls music plays, people pog. This is somewhat of an oversimplification on all sides, but I think the point is clear.

It sticks with me so much, though, because by my own measure (and forgive me for the arrogance with which this will come of), I think Lessons in Love is way better than Eternum, but hereby I am bound by the fact I can effortlessly sell people on Eternum while it's an immense struggle to even get someone to acknowledge that Lessons in Love isn't EOP trash. An easy jab here is something like 'where there's smoke there's fire' but it really goes to show the value in marketing that animated sequences and so on has. It's come to the point that when shilling Lessons in Love I link that one youtube video of the Room with Clocks somewhat begrudgingly because I've found it to be the most effective way at cracking that outer layer of doubt and mockery.

As a final word I will post a (somewhat erotically charged) screenshot of Eternum to discuss one interesting exchange I had.


There is exactly one individual whom I know who recognized LiL's quality without any artful deception and was offput by anything I shared of Eternum. This one individual is someone I respect above almost all others for his sharp mind and cutting insight, though I say this now only for performative purposes. Upon seeing the above screenshot of Eternum, they were offput because there was no physical interaction between the heroines; despite living together and mostly being a family, they were visibly posed separately and placed separately. They stare at the protagonist with ghoulish eyes and slack jaws while totally lacking cognizance for any of their family nearby. There is no sense of place or family or character here; there is only dolled-up and posed Honey Select models. Contrast this with say the former title screen and oft-referenced class photo in Lessons in Love, where Ayane hugs Sana, sana looks back at Ayane, Maya averts her eyes, Makoto has a hand on Miku, Ami has a hand placed on Makoto, and the one portion of the photo palpably unblemished, noticeably uncovered by dust, is the indeed the face of Ami looking directly at the camera, ghoulish smile on her face... That, I would say, is the level of insight it takes to appreciate Lessons in Love at a glance over Eternum. Isn't that a funny thing?

So I thought and thought and... honestly, it's not that complicated. Eternum's own shallowness is what made it so much more universally appealing at a glance, and while that seems like a salty or backhanded insult, that is not my intention. Rather, there are basically no jokes like the spaghetti, and there are minimal long-running contextual sources of humor or pog that you have to be immersed in the game to understand. Everything is immediate, direct, in-your-face, and so on. Alas, I do not believe F95 handles clips well, but I will attempt to link 3 streamable examples.

https://streamable.com/6jr2jj
https://streamable.com/1s11d8
https://streamable.com/edxxar

What we see here are instances of what in the Japanese community we refer to as "high quality 演出," with 演出 being like a mix of 'scene direction' and 'production value.' Essentially a scene that looks high-effort and good will be said to have good 演出. Anyway, what Eternum lacks in deep or meaningful characterization it has in spades in 演出, and an outside observer will need little understanding of any lore or contextual humor to appreciate this. Link a picture of an artful discussion between Nodoka and Sensei, you run a fine line of people rolling their eyes. Link a clip of the camera spinning like crazy as dark souls music plays, people pog. This is somewhat of an oversimplification on all sides, but I think the point is clear.

It sticks with me so much, though, because by my own measure (and forgive me for the arrogance with which this will come of), I think Lessons in Love is way better than Eternum, but hereby I am bound by the fact I can effortlessly sell people on Eternum while it's an immense struggle to even get someone to acknowledge that Lessons in Love isn't EOP trash. An easy jab here is something like 'where there's smoke there's fire' but it really goes to show the value in marketing that animated sequences and so on has. View attachment 4371368
View attachment 4371395

By the point I reached it I was happy just to see something written in what felt like native English, and it has nice production values to boot. The problem for me was that (as is so often the case), the character psychology ended up just a bit too underbaked to be engaging for a long period of time. The protagonist himself being a nothingburger was a big negative, but the heroines getting blander over time (or perhaps - not introducing any freshness after their introduction) was of course the real killer. A cloud of grimness fell over me as I trudged further and further into the game realizing that, far from learning more about the characters, I was simply observing the author shift gears into romance and sex mode dot exe. The clearest demonstration of this shallow writing, though, is best observed in the side characters rather than the main characters; there we consistently see cruel, bully-ish depictions of cardboard cutouts meant to be nothing more than stepping stones for the protagonist to grind the heels of his feet into. You can tell a lot about an author by how they treat side characters: are they jokes or do they feel like believable parts of the world? (With some consideration given to parodies and one-offs and so on). It is only with a roll of my eyes I point to Sara in Lessons in Love here, although I really do not want to fellate Selebus on this matter in particular: imagine a world where Sara is like a comical milf stereotype and then over 3 million words she is basically only used for sexo if not immediately forgotten.

For some extremely thought-provoking reason, almost every screenshot or clip of Lessons in Love I sent inspired ire and mockery. posts.content_html_raw:
OIUEFIU said:
Might be the first time I read one of your long posts. Cant say more, than that I agree. Also based. BTW, what was the reaction of the three japanese GAMERS who actually played Lil, to the game?
Click to expand...
One loved it so much he declared he liked it more than Subahibi despite the immense social cost that came with that (lol). He's in the process of writing a massive, artful post which I will share when he is done. He would have finished by now but he hated 0.45 and didn't want to write with seethe in his heart. (By the way, by Japanese VN readers I mean bilingual Westerners often living in Japan who mainly read Japanese VNs. Basically the opposite of WEG gamers who found LiL on itch.io and played it as their first VN. Unsurprisingly, Japanese people don't know English very well and are not interested in English-only VNs.)

One is fascinated by the denpa/plot but has a strong revulsion for all the slice of life. He considers LiL a valuable experience and is glad it was forced upon him but has little enthusiasm from the heart for it as a result. One interesting thing in his evaluation is that he hates the so-called "hivemind" of the heroines in how they are all drawn to Sensei and talk about his dick. It was comments like this that made me start thinking about the possibility of an 'actual' hivemind or 'actual' brainwashing going on of some sort, as one theory among many, which lately has gained weight due to all this rabies stuff.

One is mixed in that, let's say, he likes 50% of characters but dislikes the other 50% of characters, such that he enjoys the game and every scene with Niki etc etc but immediately wants to shoot his brains out for any scene with Miku. He is strongly a proponent that the cast should have been halved, and it's due to him that I came up with the concept of "favorite character RNG" which is the idea that one's LiL experience greatly depends on the pseudorandom chance of how much they like each member of the cast. If you like 5 and dislike 15 you're in for a bad time, if you like 15 and dislike 5 it'll be better, etc etc. He also wrote a very long essay of constructive criticism for Selebus but tossed it into the trash after determining Selebus was not someone who listens fairly to criticism (lol).

There is also a highly intellectual person who doesn't read many VNs who started not due to me brokering points but simply because they have a keen insight for literature and noticed from my screenshots the game was something special. He by far has responded to LiL the best and made it his mission for all his close friends and family to play the game. If Selebus knew this person he would probably be overjoyed, there really is no better model of a player: someone who solves puzzles entirely on their own no matter how many hours it takes, someone who sincerely considers the writing specifically to be among America's greatest (he humorously has called LiL 'the latest great American novel' or something), someone who shills the game, etc etc. Sadly, he will hear of him only indirectly in this post.


Overall not so bad considering how tough the crowd was.

One of the many phases I went through playing this game.
Found the game on itch and the first thing I did was skip through all the text to get to the first h-scene ofc :‎D and damnn, was it a lot of text. Wasnt even sure I would be able to read it.

I got around to reading from the beginning and the things I remember the most from that time are how weird Senseis model looked and I found the "happy scenes" with all the flashing pretentious, cringe and nothing burgers.

After that I got hooked on the plot of the whole world resetting and all that, so I greatly preferred Maya events, since her events moved the plot the most. I felt like the plot was absolute drip-feed with how slow it was moving. But slowly I realized that even the "slice of life" events were very entertaining and the character writing was absolute fire, so I got to liking pretty much anything the game offered.

I would guess that around chapter 2 I realized that this game was absolute cinema and that I wont be able to ever find something similar to this. Got myself completely swallowed by the story and characters.

Then I guess the final stage would be when I started to like every character around the end of chapter 3. Till that point I still had some that I found at least boring (Tsuneyo).

posts.content_html_raw:
PrincessEuphy said:
One loved it so much he declared he liked it more than Subahibi despite the immense social cost that came with that (lol). He's in the process of writing a massive, artful post which I will share when he is done. He would have finished by now but he hated 0.45 and didn't want to write with seethe in his heart. (By the way, by Japanese VN readers I mean bilingual Westerners often living in Japan who mainly read Japanese VNs. Basically the opposite of WEG gamers who found LiL on itch.io and played it as their first VN. Unsurprisingly, Japanese people don't know English very well and are not interested in English-only VNs.)

One is fascinated by the denpa/plot but has a strong revulsion for all the slice of life. He considers LiL a valuable experience and is glad it was forced upon him but has little enthusiasm from the heart for it as a result. One interesting thing in his evaluation is that he hates the so-called "hivemind" of the heroines in how they are all drawn to Sensei and talk about his dick. It was comments like this that made me start thinking about the possibility of an 'actual' hivemind or 'actual' brainwashing going on of some sort, as one theory among many, which lately has gained weight due to all this rabies stuff.

One is mixed in that, let's say, he likes 50% of characters but dislikes the other 50% of characters, such that he enjoys the game and every scene with Niki etc etc but immediately wants to shoot his brains out for any scene with Miku. He is strongly a proponent that the cast should have been halved, and it's due to him that I came up with the concept of "favorite character RNG" which is the idea that one's LiL experience greatly depends on the pseudorandom chance of how much they like each member of the cast. If you like 5 and dislike 15 you're in for a bad time, if you like 15 and dislike 5 it'll be better, etc etc. He also wrote a very long essay of constructive criticism for Selebus but tossed it into the trash after determining Selebus was not someone who listens fairly to criticism (lol).

There is also a highly intellectual person who doesn't read many VNs who started not due to me brokering points but simply because they have a keen insight for literature and noticed from my screenshots the game was something special. He by far has responded to LiL the best and made it his mission for all his close friends and family to play the game. If Selebus knew this person he would probably be overjoyed, there really is no better model of a player: someone who solves puzzles entirely on their own no matter how many hours it takes, someone who sincerely considers the writing specifically to be among America's greatest (he humorously has called LiL 'the latest great American novel' or something), someone who shills the game, etc etc. Sadly, he will hear of him only indirectly in this post.


Overall not so bad considering how tough the crowd was.
Click to expand...
Well who could guess that there are really Japanese reading LiL lol. Despite being fully American novel and writing style, I could argue some thinking and ideas in LiL is quite oriental thus it didn't come that much of a surprise. Though rather than Subahibi with which each Denpa visual novel seems inevitably have to compare. Some of the ramblings and reminds me of Kyojin-tachi which experiences more on language and subjectivity of fictional characters and authenticity of game or any medium themselves while ruthlessly unveiling intrusion of author to every visible pore of the game.

I would call LiL as the greatest post-modernism American novel had it not been such a conceitful and self-righteous author. Let's not concern my congenial prejudice on English novels and favor on classical Russian ones here first.

OIUEFIU said:
One of the many phases I went through playing this game.
Found the game on itch and the first thing I did was skip through all the text to get to the first h-scene ofc :‎D and damnn, was it a lot of text. Wasnt even sure I would be able to read it.

I got around to reading from the beginning and the things I remember the most from that time are how weird Senseis model looked and I found the "happy scenes" with all the flashing pretentious, cringe and nothing burgers.

After that I got hooked on the plot of the whole world resetting and all that, so I greatly preferred Maya events, since her events moved the plot the most. I felt like the plot was absolute drip-feed with how slow it was moving. But slowly I realized that even the "slice of life" events were very entertaining and the character writing was absolute fire, so I got to liking pretty much anything the game offered.

I would guess that around chapter 2 I realized that this was game absolute cinema and that I wont be able to ever find something similar to this. Got myself completely swallowed by the story and characters.

Then I guess the final stage would be when I started to like every character around the end of chapter 3. Till that point I still had some that I found at least boring (Tsuneyo).
Click to expand...
The only phase I had was my sardonic enjoyment transitioning to sincere enjoyment over the first chapter once I realized it was purposefully good rather than accidentally good. I never really "like" or "dislike" characters so much as evaluate their depth and execution. The idea of disliking a character is beyond me; if I find myself displeased by their scenes, I will first attribute it to a failure of the author for failing to depict them correctly, though that of course is purely a psychological construction of my own making. E.g. for Eternum it's not like I dislike Dalia or Annie, I just feel like they were written shallowly, for example. So from the start I 'liked' all characters in LiL and continue to like them all, although Kaori's particular way of speaking gives me a headache.

Then I guess the final stage would be when I started to like every character around the end of chapter 3. Till that point I still had some that I found at least boring (Tsuneyo).
Click to expand...
The only phase I had was my sardonic enjoyment transitioning to sincere enjoyment over the first chapter once I realized it was purposefully good rather than accidentally good. I never really "like" or "dislike" characters so much as evaluate their depth and execution. The idea of disliking a character is beyond me; if I find myself displeased by their scenes, I will first attribute it to a failure of the author for failing to depict them correctly, though that of course is purely a psychological construction of my own making. E.g. for Eternum it's not like I dislike Dalia or Annie, I just feel like they were written shallowly, for example. So from the start I 'liked' all characters in LiL and continue to like them all, although Kaori's particular way of speaking gives me a headache.

Tierlist and character notes and rules.

Being in the "not my type" tier is not necessarily fair but it's less work. Below that tier just means I haven't built a mental profile on the character yet. Children are measured by how fun they are to be around and how adorable they are, overlooking any other factor.

I don't hate any of the characters, I may just find them unremarkable and boring or can't see myself physically attracted to them.

The further top left the character is, the more I like them. Heavily affected by momentary bias.

If I didn't mention someone here, I probably don't have anything noteworthy to say yet.

Tierlists are hard, so the rankings may not be quite accurate to my true emotions and changes over time.

Sex scenes may affect where they are positioned based on momentary bias.

If the color of the tiles are the same, it means they are equally important.

I may forgive characters over time for a past mistake, bumping them back up.

spoilers.title: Tierlist
spoilers.html:
Tierlist and character notes and rules.

Being in the "not my type" tier is not necessarily fair but it's less work. Below that tier just means I haven't built a mental profile on the character yet. Children are measured by how fun they are to be around and how adorable they are, overlooking any other factor.

I don't hate any of the characters, I may just find them unremarkable and boring or can't see myself physically attracted to them.

The further top left the character is, the more I like them. Heavily affected by momentary bias.

If I didn't mention someone here, I probably don't have anything noteworthy to say yet.

Tierlists are hard, so the rankings may not be quite accurate to my true emotions and changes over time.

Sex scenes may affect where they are positioned based on momentary bias.

If the color of the tiles are the same, it means they are equally important.

I may forgive characters over time for a past mistake, bumping them back up.

A character most likely won't lose their position just because I haven't seen them enough in a while.

posts.content_html_raw:
The confusion probably derives from people not understanding what the purity routes are supposed to be.

So when we say we're at the middle of chapter 4 and there are 6 chapters (and that one should be the shorter one), one would assume we're way past 50%.

However, the purity routes are individual routes for each and every character that come after chapter 6 (the dark route). Even if it's one purity route per month, we're talking years here since, again, it's one per character.

The counterpoint would be that if you're interested in, say, Chika's ending, and that's the first purity route we get, then you can close the game by then and we're certainly closer to that (the first ending) than we are to the last purity route, or the true ending. By a matter of years. So we should be getting some closure sooner than the actual final closure of the true end.
